description: DEF CON 33 Main Stage features the conference's headline presentations, keynotes, and technical security research across hardware, cloud, AI, and offensive tradecraft. Sessions cover silicon exploitation, Active Directory attack paths, kernel vulnerabilities, zero-day research, and critical discussions on privacy and policy.

talks.title: DisguiseDelimit: Exploiting Synology NAS with S2S and Pre-Auth RCE Chains
talks.teaser: Discloses a pre-authentication remote code execution chain against Synology DSM, demonstrating how attackers achieve root compromise via the S2S protocol.
talks.summary:
Synology Network-Attached Storage Attack Surface

Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) devices serve as central storage and application servers for enterprise and home networks. Exposing these appliances to the internet creates an attractive target for initial access brokers and ransomware operators.

Flaws in the Site-to-Site Protocol

Nassim Asrir and Zackary Flack identify critical vulnerabilities within the Synology Site-to-Site (S2S) communication protocol and authentication handlers. Insecure delimiter parsing and state confusion allow unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass access controls.

Chaining to Pre-Auth Remote Root Execution

By chaining parser differentials with memory corruption flaws in backend daemons, researchers achieve pre-authentication remote code execution with root privileges, bypassing system sandboxes.

Remediation and Defense for Storage Appliances

Securing network-attached storage infrastructure requires disabling external management exposure, applying vendor firmware patches promptly, and isolating storage management networks behind dedicated VPNs.

talks.title: Browser Extension Clickjacking: One Click and Your Cloud Is Pwned
talks.teaser: Exposes UI redressing and clickjacking vectors in popular browser extensions that trick users into granting administrative cloud permissions with a single click.
talks.summary:
Browser Extensions as an Overlooked Threat Vector

Browser extensions operate with elevated privileges within web browsers, frequently interacting with active cloud sessions, password managers, and enterprise SaaS dashboards.

Clickjacking and UI Redressing Mechanics

Lior Shmueli and Tomer Peled demonstrate how malicious web pages leverage CSS opacity layering and iframe positioning to execute clickjacking attacks against browser extension popup interfaces.

Account Takeovers and Cloud Role Escalation

By manipulating users into clicking seemingly innocuous page elements, attackers trigger privileged actions inside extensions—such as exporting credentials, approving OAuth authorizations, or delegating cloud IAM roles.

Hardening Extension UI Boundaries

Mitigating extension clickjacking requires browser vendors and developers to enforce CSP frame-ancestors directives, require explicit confirmation dialogues for high-privilege actions, and validate user intent.

talks.title: Can't Stop the ROP: Automating Universal ASLR Bypass and ROP Generation
talks.teaser: Presents an automated framework for generating universal return-oriented programming chains and bypassing ASLR across modern operating system binaries.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Return-Oriented Programming

Modern exploit mitigation technologies, such as Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) and Data Execution Prevention (DEP), require exploit developers to construct intricate Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) chains to execute arbitrary code.

Automating Gadget Discovery and State Tracking

Tim Becker introduces an automated exploitation framework that parses binary disassembled code, tracks register state transitions, and stitches together robust ROP gadgets across target memory spaces.

Universal ASLR Bypass Techniques

The framework leverages memory disclosure primitives and partial pointer overwrites to defeat ASLR dynamically, constructing functional ROP chains without prior knowledge of base addresses.

Implications for Exploit Mitigation Engineering

Automated ROP synthesis demonstrates that traditional runtime protections must be augmented with fine-grained control-flow integrity (CFI), memory tagging, and memory-safe language adoption.

talks.title: Breakin 'Em All: Overcoming Pokemon Go's Anti-Cheat and Reverse Engineering
talks.teaser: Deconstructs the anti-cheat and runtime integrity mechanisms in Pokemon Go, demonstrating mobile reverse engineering and integrity bypass tradecraft.
talks.summary:
Mobile Anti-Cheat Architecture

Mobile location-based games deploy multi-layered anti-tamper and anti-cheat mechanisms to protect game economies and prevent GPS spoofing and automated botting.

Reverse Engineering Obfuscated Mobile Binaries

Hugo Gonzalez and Caleb Howell analyze native libraries, dynamic code loading routines, and heavily obfuscated integrity verification functions protecting mobile game clients.

Bypassing Runtime Environment Checks

Researchers demonstrate how to circumvent jailbreak and root detection, Frida hooking checks, and Play Integrity attestations by patching native binary routines and intercepting system calls.

Lessons for Mobile Application Protection

Analyzing game anti-cheat ecosystems highlights the continuous cat-and-mouse dynamic between mobile application protectors and reverse engineers.

talks.title: BitUnlocker: Leverage Windows Recovery to Extract BitLocker Keys
talks.teaser: Demonstrates physical and firmware attack vectors against Windows Recovery environments to extract BitLocker encryption keys from TPM and memory.
talks.summary:
BitLocker Full-Disk Encryption Foundations

Microsoft BitLocker secures enterprise endpoints by sealing full-disk encryption keys within the hardware Trusted Platform Module (TPM) and validating boot integrity.

Attacking the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE)

David Ledbetter details how physical access to Windows endpoints during WinRE boot sequences exposes diagnostic interfaces and unencrypted memory regions containing keying material.

Sniffing TPM Buses and Memory Extraction

Attaching hardware logic analyzers to LPC or SPI buses during boot allows researchers to intercept plaintext BitLocker Volume Master Keys (VMK) transmitted between the discrete TPM and CPU.

Defensive Hardening for Enterprise Laptops

Mitigating physical BitLocker key extraction requires enabling TPM with startup PINs, deploying integrated/firmware TPMs (fTPM), and restricting WinRE execution.

talks.title: Gateways to Chaos: How We Proved Modems Are Cellular Backdoors
talks.teaser: Reveals critical baseband and firmware vulnerabilities in popular cellular modems that allow remote over-the-air exploitation and device takeover.
talks.summary:
The Cellular Baseband Attack Surface

Cellular modems embedded in laptops, routers, and IoT gateways process complex over-the-air radio signaling stacks independently of host operating systems.

Reverse Engineering Modem Firmware

Researchers reverse engineer proprietary baseband RTOS firmware, uncovering memory corruption vulnerabilities in cellular radio resource control (RRC) and SMS message parsing engines.

Over-the-Air Remote Code Execution

Transmitting malformed cellular packets from a software-defined radio base station triggers unauthenticated remote code execution on the modem core, establishing persistent backdoors beneath host OS visibility.

Securing the Cellular Edge

Protecting cellular devices requires modem vendors to implement memory-safe baseband parsers, enforce secure boot on cellular microcontrollers, and isolate baseband buses via hardware IOMMUs.

talks.title: New Red Team Networking Techniques for Initial Access and Evasion
talks.teaser: Introduces advanced offensive networking techniques and covert communication channels to bypass modern enterprise perimeter monitoring and EDR telemetry.
talks.summary:
Modern Perimeter Monitoring Challenges

Enterprise security operations deploy sophisticated Network Detection and Response (NDR) and EDR telemetry pipelines to identify anomalous outbound connections and known command-and-control signatures.

Covert C2 Communication Tradecraft

Jason Lang demonstrates novel networking primitives that blend command-and-control traffic with legitimate cloud services, legitimate CDN fronting, and obscure network protocols to evade traffic inspection.

Bypassing Network Access Controls and Egress Filters

Techniques for leveraging IPv6 tunneling, protocol multiplexing, and dynamic egress routing allow red teamers to establish resilient initial access footholds in highly monitored environments.

Detection Strategies for Blue Teams

Defenders improve visibility by analyzing protocol timing anomalies, inspecting encrypted traffic metadata (JA4), and correlating network flows with host process telemetry.

talks.title: Ghost Calls: Abusing Web Conferencing for Covert C2 and Exfiltration
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how WebRTC channels and enterprise web conferencing platforms can be repurposed as stealthy command-and-control and data exfiltration pipelines.
talks.summary:
The Rise of WebRTC and Collaboration Platforms

Enterprise organizations widely permit encrypted WebRTC and web conferencing traffic across corporate firewalls to support remote communication and collaboration.

Repurposing WebRTC Data Channels for C2

Gal Weizman shows how red teams can establish bi-directional, peer-to-peer WebRTC data channels through legitimate conferencing infrastructure to execute stealthy command-and-control operations.

Data Exfiltration via Encrypted Media Streams

Encoding stolen enterprise data into WebRTC audio/video streams or steganographic metadata bypasses standard Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and deep packet inspection proxies.

Defending Enterprise Collaboration Boundaries

Mitigating web conferencing abuse requires organizations to monitor WebRTC connection endpoints, restrict unauthorized browser extension permissions, and inspect application-layer session telemetry.

talks.title: Carding, Sabotage & Survival: A Darknet Market Case Study
talks.teaser: Examines the internal operations, financial infrastructure, and sabotage tactics behind major underground darknet carding markets.
talks.summary:
Inside the Darknet Market Ecosystem

Illicit underground markets trade millions of stolen payment cards, compromised credentials, and financial databases, operating complex technical ecosystems resilient to law enforcement takedowns.

Operational Infrastructure and Escrow Mechanics

Alex Holden provides a case study of darknet market operations, analyzing their multi-tiered server infrastructure, automated cryptocurrency escrow systems, and merchant vetting procedures.

Inter-Cartel Sabotage and Cyber Warfare

Darknet market administrators frequently engage in ruthless sabotage campaigns against rival platforms, leveraging massive DDoS botnets, database leaks, and extortion to eliminate competition.

Threat Intelligence and Law Enforcement Disruption

Tracking market infrastructure and financial flows provides actionable threat intelligence, enabling cybersecurity researchers and law enforcement to map criminal syndicates and protect consumer accounts.

talks.title: Building a Malware Museum: Preserving Digital Threat History
talks.teaser: Mikko Hypponen explores the preservation of historic malware samples, early virus artistry, and four decades of digital threats in the Malware Museum.
talks.summary:
The Cultural and Technical History of Computer Viruses

Early computer malware from the MS-DOS era was often crafted by hobbyists and pranksters, featuring elaborate visual effects, chiptune music, and creative screen animations rather than financial extortion payloads.

Curating and Emulating Historic Malware

Mikko Hypponen details the creation of the Malware Museum, using browser-based DOSBox emulation to safely demonstrate historic viruses—such as Brain, Cascade, and Ambulance—without risking infectious spread.

Evolution Toward Weaponization and Cybercrime

Tracking the timeline from 1980s floppy disk boot sector infectors to modern state-sponsored wipers and multi-million-dollar ransomware cartels illustrates the radical transformation of malware economics.

Preserving Hacker Culture and Threat Artifacts

Documenting early malware artifacts ensures that digital security history, vintage reverse engineering techniques, and early hacker subcultures remain accessible for future generations of security researchers.

talks.title: 7 Vulns in 7 Days: Breaking Bloatware Faster Than Vendors Can Ship
talks.teaser: Demonstrates rapid vulnerability discovery methodologies that uncovered seven zero-day local privilege escalation flaws in pre-installed OEM bloatware.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Pre-Installed OEM Software

Consumer and enterprise laptops ship with pre-installed OEM support tools and diagnostic utilities. These privileged background services frequently introduce critical vulnerabilities.

Rapid Vulnerability Discovery Methodology

Julian Horoszkiewicz outlines a fast-paced auditing approach that uncovered seven separate local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in OEM software suites within a single week.

Exploiting Insecure IPC, Named Pipes, and Services

Common flaw patterns include unauthenticated named pipe commands, DLL hijacking in SYSTEM services, and flawed registry permissions that allow low-privilege users to execute code as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

Remediation and OEM Supply Chain Hygiene

Eliminating bloatware risks requires hardware vendors to minimize pre-installed software, enforce strict service access control lists, and undergo rigorous third-party security audits prior to device imaging.

talks.title: Thinking Like a Hacker in the Age of AI
talks.teaser: Bruce Schneier examines how artificial intelligence systems find and exploit legal, economic, and societal vulnerabilities, transforming the nature of hacking.
talks.summary:
Expanding the Definition of Hacking

Hacking is fundamentally about finding unintended vulnerabilities and subverting complex rule-based systems. While traditionally applied to computer code, hacking extends to tax codes, financial regulations, and political processes.

Artificial Intelligence as Autonomous Hackers

Bruce Schneier explores how AI systems with high-speed computational analysis will autonomously identify loopholes in legal statutes, corporate governance, and market regulations far faster than human legislators can close them.

Societal and Economic Ramifications

AI-driven optimization of societal systems introduces risks of systemic gaming, where automated algorithms exploit financial markets, legal contracts, and social platforms for concentrated private gain.

Governance and Defensive Policy Frameworks

Adapting to AI-scale vulnerabilities requires agile governance models, transparent algorithmic decision-making, and rapid legislative patching mechanisms.

talks.title: Recording PCAPs from Stingrays With a $20 Hotspot
talks.teaser: Shows how modifying an inexpensive consumer 4G LTE mobile hotspot allows researchers to capture raw network packets and detect IMSI catcher surveillance.
talks.summary:
Cellular Interception via IMSI Catchers

IMSI catchers (commonly referred to as Stingrays or cell-site simulators) pose severe privacy and surveillance threats by spoofing cellular base stations to track mobile devices and intercept communications.

Modifying Inexpensive Consumer Hotspots

Cooper Quintin and Yomna Nasser demonstrate how modifying a $20 off-the-shelf mobile Wi-Fi hotspot enables raw cellular frame capture and logging directly to PCAP files.

Detecting Rogue Cellular Base Station Anomalies

Analyzing captured packet traces reveals distinct IMSI catcher signatures, including forced cipher downgrades, unexpected cell reselection parameters, and abnormal identity request sequences.

Empowering Grassroots Surveillance Defense

Releasing open-source firmware tools empowers civil liberties researchers, journalists, and activists to monitor and document illicit cellular surveillance in public spaces.

talks.title: Winners of DARPA’s AI Cyber Challenge
talks.teaser: Finalists from DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge present autonomous cyber reasoning systems designed to find, patch, and remediate critical software vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
The DARPA AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC)

DARPA launched the AI Cyber Challenge to spur the development of next-generation Cyber Reasoning Systems (CRS) that combine artificial intelligence with automated program analysis to secure critical open-source software.

Autonomous Vulnerability Discovery and Patching

Competing teams showcase CRS architectures that automatically analyze complex C, C++, and Java codebases, discover zero-day vulnerabilities, and generate verified, non-breaking security patches in real time.

Integrating LLMs with Dynamic Analysis Tools

The winning systems integrate large language models with fuzzing engines (such as AFL++ and libFuzzer), symbolic execution frameworks, and automated regression testbeds to eliminate false positives.

The Future of Automated Software Defense

Automating vulnerability discovery and patch deployment transforms software defense, enabling rapid remediation of supply chain vulnerabilities before adversaries can weaponize them.

talks.title: Help! Linux in My Webcam!
talks.teaser: Demonstrates hardware hacking and reverse engineering to run custom Linux kernels and open software on inexpensive USB webcams.
talks.summary:
Embedded Hardware Inside Consumer Webcams

Modern high-definition USB webcams often contain powerful multi-core ARM or RISC-V system-on-chips capable of running full operating systems.

Reverse Engineering Webcam PCB Interfaces

Jeroen Domburg analyzes board traces, test points, and SPI flash memory chips on commercial webcams, identifying UART debug headers and bootloader configuration pins.

Compiling Custom Linux and U-Boot

By porting U-Boot and modern Linux kernels to the webcam's embedded SoC, researchers convert inexpensive cameras into standalone network devices capable of running on-device computer vision algorithms.

Open Hardware and Re-Purposing Electronics

Hacking consumer camera hardware promotes electronics sustainability, open-source hardware re-use, and demystifies low-level embedded Linux system bring-up.

talks.title: Breaking Wi-Fi Easy Connect: A Security Analysis of DPP
talks.teaser: Conducts a comprehensive security analysis of Wi-Fi Easy Connect (Device Provisioning Protocol v3.0), uncovering protocol design flaws and implementation vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Wi-Fi Easy Connect (DPP) Architecture

Wi-Fi Easy Connect, standardized by the Wi-Fi Alliance as the Device Provisioning Protocol (DPP), is designed to replace insecure Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) using QR codes, NFC, and public-key cryptography for IoT provisioning.

Protocol Analysis and Cryptographic Flaws

George Chatzisofroniou presents an in-depth security evaluation of DPP version 3.0, identifying vulnerabilities in cryptographic key exchange handshakes and mutual authentication routines.

Attacking Unauthenticated Configuration Channels

Design flaws allow nearby wireless adversaries to intercept provisioning frames, conduct denial-of-service attacks, or manipulate device configuration parameters during initial onboarding.

Recommendations for Wi-Fi Alliance Standards

Remediating Wi-Fi Easy Connect flaws requires updating the protocol specification to mandate strict public key validation and enforce timeout thresholds on provisioning sessions.

talks.title: Turning Your Active Directory into the Attacker’s C2
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how red teams can weaponize Active Directory Group Policy Objects (GPOs) into a stealthy, native command-and-control infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Active Directory as Centralized Infrastructure

Active Directory (AD) is designed to coordinate and manage enterprise computers, users, and security settings across distributed corporate networks.

Weaponizing Group Policy Objects for C2

Quentin Roland and Wilfried Bécard show how attackers who obtain GPO modification rights can repurpose Group Policy replication into a covert command-and-control mechanism that requires no external network connections.

Persistence and Privilege Escalation Across Network Segments

By embedding scheduled tasks, script execution policies, and immediate task items within replicated GPO templates, operators distribute commands to thousands of domain-joined systems simultaneously.

Detecting Malicious GPO Manipulation

Defending Active Directory against GPO weaponization requires monitoring directory replication logs, enforcing tiered administration models, and auditing GPO permissions.

talks.title: Exploiting Vulns in EV Charging Comms
talks.teaser: Discloses vulnerabilities in QCA 7000 HomePlug modems used across CCS and NACS EV charging systems that enable communication hijacking and denial of service.
talks.summary:
Power-Line Communication in EV Charging Infrastructure

Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems rely on Combined Charging System (CCS) and North American Charging Standard (NACS) protocols, which utilize HomePlug Green PHY power-line communication (PLC) for vehicle-to-grid data exchange.

Vulnerabilities in the QCA 7000 Modem Series

Jan Berens, Marcell Szakály, and Sebastian Köhler analyze the widely used Qualcomm QCA 7000 modem series, uncovering multiple critical vulnerabilities in PLC message processing and firmware execution.

Remote Communication Hijacking and Denial of Service

Exploiting flaws in HomePlug link negotiation allows attackers to intercept charging session telemetry at a distance, inject spoofed control commands, or trigger persistent denial-of-service conditions that prevent vehicle charging.

Firmware Reverse Engineering and Code Execution

Reverse engineering the QCA 7000 firmware revealed memory corruption vulnerabilities enabling arbitrary code execution on the modem hardware, highlighting urgent security needs across global EV charging infrastructure.

talks.title: Journey to the Center of PSTN: I Became a Phone Company. You Should Too
talks.teaser: Demystifies the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN), explaining how to establish a licensed telecommunications carrier to explore telecom routing and SS7.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Infrastructure of the PSTN

The Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) underpins global voice communication, yet its regulatory and technical architecture remains largely opaque to security researchers.

Becoming a Licensed Telecom Carrier

Enzo Damato details the technical and bureaucratic process of registering as a legitimate competitive local exchange carrier (CLEC) to gain direct interconnection with global telecom carriers.

Exploring SS7, SIP Interconnects, and Call Routing

Direct carrier interconnection grants access to raw SS7 signaling links, SIP trunking exchanges, and Caller ID databases, exposing fundamental vulnerabilities in telephone authentication and routing.

Telecommunications Security and Policy Implications

Understanding the inner workings of carrier networks enables researchers to identify telecom fraud, caller-ID spoofing, and advocate for cryptographic caller authentication standards (STIR/SHAKEN).

talks.title: Amber64: Mining Hacker History from Over 500k Commodore 64 Disks
talks.teaser: Wesley McGrew analyzes digital forensics and unallocated space across 500,000 Commodore 64 floppy disk images to uncover early hacker subcultures and ephemera.
talks.summary:
Digital Archaeology of the Commodore 64 Era

The Commodore 64 was central to the early hacker, phreaker, and software cracking subcultures of the 1980s and 1990s.

Forensic Ingestion of 500,000 Disk Images

Wesley McGrew created the Amber64 project, ingesting and parsing hundreds of thousands of digitized C64 floppy disk images using modern digital forensics and data mining pipelines.

Recovering Unallocated Ephemera and BBS Messages

Analyzing unallocated sectors and deleted file fragments revealed preserved BBS communications, hacker group handles, custom crack intros, and unreleased source code preserved in digital amber.

Preserving Computer Security History

Applying structured digital forensics to retro computing artifacts provides unique historical insights into the origins of modern cybersecurity tradecraft and hacker culture.

talks.title: Win-DoS Epidemic: Abusing RPC for Win-DoS & Win-DDoS
talks.teaser: Discloses new remote denial-of-service vulnerabilities in Windows RPC and Active Directory that enable cascading Win-DoS and Win-DDoS epidemics across Domain Controllers.
talks.summary:
The Criticality of Domain Controllers in Enterprise Security

Active Directory Domain Controllers (DCs) serve as the core identity and authentication backbone for enterprise networks. Taking down DCs paralyzes organizational operations.

Discovering New RPC Denial-of-Service Vulnerabilities

Building upon their LDAPNightmare research (CVE-2024-49113), Or Yair and Shahak Morag identify multiple novel denial-of-service vulnerabilities in Windows Remote Procedure Call (RPC) and Active Directory services.

Creating the Win-DoS and Win-DDoS Epidemic

Attackers can trigger memory corruption and infinite processing loops on target DCs, inducing them to forward malformed RPC requests to secondary DCs and forming a self-propagating denial-of-service wave.

Hardening Windows RPC and Domain Controller Defenses

Mitigating RPC-based DoS epidemics requires applying Microsoft security updates, restricting RPC endpoint binding, and isolating Domain Controller interfaces behind internal firewalls.

talks.title: ReVault! Compromised by Your Secure SoC
talks.teaser: Demonstrates the ReVault hardware attack targeting secure microcontrollers embedded across over 100 enterprise laptop models to compromise master keys.
talks.summary:
Trust Assumptions in Secure Microcontrollers

Modern enterprise laptops integrate dedicated security chips and secure microcontrollers to store disk encryption keys, biometric credentials, and administrative passwords.

The ReVault Hardware Attack Chain

Philippe Laulheret presents ReVault, an attack targeting proprietary security microcontrollers embedded in over 100 enterprise laptop models, demonstrating how low-privilege attackers can bypass silicon-level protections.

Extracting Sealed Secrets and Firmware Flaws

Analyzing firmware execution and physical bus interactions reveals vulnerabilities in secure boot and memory isolation, enabling unauthorized extraction of sealed cryptographic keys.

Hardware Hardening for Endpoint Silicon

Mitigating secure SoC compromises demands hardware-enforced memory encryption, authenticated firmware updates, and rigorous silicon-level vulnerability testing.

talks.title: How to Secure Unique Ecosystem Shipping 1 Billion+ Cores?
talks.teaser: Details the security architecture and defensive engineering required to secure NVIDIA's transition of the Falcon microprocessor to RISC-V across billions of GPU cores.
talks.summary:
Scaling Security Across Billion-Core Architectures

NVIDIA's proprietary microprocessors control GPU hardware initialization, power management, and secure enclave isolation across billions of deployed chips worldwide.

Transitioning Falcon to RISC-V Architecture

Adam Zabrocki and Marko Mitic detail NVIDIA’s multi-year engineering initiative transitioning internal Falcon microcontrollers to a hardened RISC-V architecture deployed at massive scale.

Hardware-Enforced Security and Cryptographic Boot

Securing custom silicon architectures requires hardware-enforced memory isolation, cryptographic boot verification, and real-time execution monitoring inside GPU firmware.

Lessons for Custom Silicon Security

Engineering custom processor architectures at planetary scale requires integrating automated formal verification, hardware fuzzing, and resilient firmware update mechanisms.

talks.title: LLM Identifies Info Stealer Vector & Extracts IoCs
talks.teaser: Demonstrates leveraging multimodal LLMs to analyze millions of infostealer infection screenshots and autonomously extract indicators of compromise.
talks.summary:
The Threat of Information Stealer Malware

Information stealer malware families (such as RedLine, Lumma, and Vidar) harvest millions of credentials, session cookies, and browser tokens daily, flooding underground cybercrime markets.

Mining Stealer Screenshot Logs

Infostealers frequently capture desktop screenshots at the moment of infection. Analyzing these visual artifacts reveals the exact infection vector, open browser tabs, and malicious download sources.

Automating Multimodal LLM Extraction Pipelines

Olivier Bilodeau and Estelle Ruellan introduce an automated processing pipeline using vision-capable LLMs to parse millions of infection screenshots, classify attack vectors, and extract Indicators of Compromise (IoCs).

Actionable Telemetry for Threat Intelligence

Deploying AI-driven screenshot analysis accelerates threat attribution, identifies active malvertising campaigns, and produces high-fidelity threat intelligence at scale.

talks.title: AutoDetection & Exploitation of DOM Clobbering Vuln at Scale
talks.teaser: Introduces Hulk, the first dynamic analysis tool to automatically detect and generate exploit payloads for complex DOM Clobbering vulnerabilities at web scale.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of DOM Clobbering

DOM Clobbering is a code-reuse web vulnerability where attackers use HTML markup to override global JavaScript variables and document properties, transforming benign scripts into Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vectors.

Systematizing DOM Clobbering Exploitation

Zhengyu Liu and Jianjia Yu present a four-stage framework modeling DOM Clobbering primitives, including named attribute collisions, collection nesting, and prototype chain manipulation.

Hulk: Automated Dynamic Analysis and Payload Generation

The authors introduce Hulk, an open-source dynamic analysis tool that crawls web applications, identifies vulnerable DOM access patterns, and automatically synthesizes working clobbering payloads.

Securing Modern Web Applications

Preventing DOM Clobbering requires web developers to avoid implicit global lookups, use Object.freeze() on critical configurations, and deploy modern HTML sanitizers (such as DOMPurify).

talks.title: Playing Dirty w/o Cheating - Getting Banned for Fun
talks.teaser: Investigates anti-cheat detection heuristics and server-side validation flaws across competitive online games, revealing how unusual play triggers bans.
talks.summary:
Anti-Cheat Detection Heuristics and Telemetry

Competitive online video games deploy server-side behavioral analysis and client-side anti-cheat drivers to detect aimbots, wallhacks, and unauthorized memory modifications.

Manipulating Behavioral and Network Heuristics

Researchers analyze how game servers evaluate player inputs, camera movement acceleration, and network packet timing. By generating mathematically valid but statistically abnormal input sequences without memory modification, players can deliberately trigger false-positive cheat bans.

Protocol Reverse Engineering and Input Edge Cases

Deconstructing game networking protocols demonstrates flaws in server-side state validation, where unoptimized physics engines misclassify complex legitimate maneuvers as automated exploits.

Improving Detection Accuracy and Fair Play

Enhancing anti-cheat systems requires developers to combine statistical thresholding with contextual gameplay verification to reduce false-positive bans.

talks.title: One Key, Two Key, I Just Stole Your goTenna Key
talks.teaser: Discloses cryptographic and firmware vulnerabilities in goTenna Pro mesh networking devices, allowing off-grid key extraction and message decryption.
talks.summary:
Off-Grid Tactical Mesh Networking with goTenna

goTenna Pro devices provide encrypted, off-grid mesh communications for defense, law enforcement, and emergency response teams operating in denied communications environments.

Reverse Engineering Firmware and Cryptographic Keystores

Erwin Karincic and Woody analyze the device firmware and hardware interfaces, uncovering critical implementation flaws in how cryptographic keys are derived, stored, and verified in memory.

Extracting Group Keys and Decrypting Mesh Telemetry

Exploiting improper key isolation and weak nonce generation enables attackers to extract pre-shared encryption keys over the air, decrypting situational awareness data and forging tactical messages.

Securing Tactical Communications Hardware

Mitigating mesh key extraction requires deploying tamper-resistant secure elements, enforcing hardware-backed key derivation, and patching over-the-air protocol handshakes.

talks.title: Metal-as-a-Disservice: Exploiting Legacy Flaws in Cutting Edge Clouds
talks.teaser: Demonstrates cross-tenant attacks and persistent firmware backdooring in major bare-metal cloud providers by exploiting legacy Baseboard Management Controllers.
talks.summary:
Bare-Metal Cloud Architecture and Multi-Tenancy

Cloud providers offer bare-metal server instances granting customers dedicated access to physical server hardware. However, ensuring clean isolation between successive tenants requires complete hardware sanitization.

Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) Vulnerabilities

Bill Demirkapi reveals critical firmware vulnerabilities in legacy BMC implementations (such as IPMI and proprietary management chips) that survive standard tenant de-provisioning workflows.

Cross-Tenant Persistence and Hypervisor Compromise

Attackers who rent bare-metal instances can flash malicious BMC firmware implants that persist across customer re-provisioning, granting unauthorized access to the next tenant’s memory, hypervisor, and data.

Securing Cloud Bare-Metal Provisioning

Hardening bare-metal clouds requires cloud operators to enforce cryptographic hardware root of trust, physically re-flash all microcontroller firmware between rentals, and isolate BMC networks.

talks.title: AppleStorm: Unmasking the Privacy Risks of Apple Intelligence
talks.teaser: Analyzes the architecture of Apple Intelligence and Private Cloud Compute, identifying privacy risks and data leakage vectors across on-device and cloud models.
talks.summary:
Apple Intelligence and Private Cloud Compute

Apple Intelligence integrates on-device generative AI models with Private Cloud Compute (PCC) to execute complex natural language tasks while maintaining strict user privacy guarantees.

Architectural Analysis of On-Device AI Routing

Yoav Magid evaluates the client-side decision-making algorithms that route user prompts and context between local neural engines and remote cloud compute clusters.

Data Exposure and Cross-App Context Leakage

Security analysis uncovers edge-case vulnerabilities where semantic indexing pipelines and app intent handlers inadvertently expose sensitive user context across unprivileged third-party apps.

Hardening Confidential AI Architectures

Ensuring absolute privacy in hybrid AI architectures requires verifiable remote cryptographic attestation, strict on-device data redaction, and independent security auditing of serverless inference nodes.

talks.title: 'We Are Currently Clean on OPSEC': The Signalgate Saga
talks.teaser: Micah Lee recounts the Signalgate investigation, dissecting mobile forensic extraction techniques, operational security failures, and secure messaging tradecraft.
talks.summary:
The Intersection of Secure Messaging and Operational Security

Signal and end-to-end encrypted messaging apps provide strong cryptographic guarantees for data in transit. However, operational security (OPSEC) failures and endpoint compromises frequently undermine user privacy.

Dissecting the Signalgate Forensic Extractions

Micah Lee details the forensic investigation into the Signalgate leaks, analyzing how mobile forensic extraction tools (such as Cellebrite) recovered unencrypted chat databases directly from compromised physical devices.

Common OPSEC Misconceptions and Failures

Examining user assumptions regarding disappearing messages, local database encryption, cloud backups, and screenshot capture reveals critical gaps in everyday privacy practices.

Best Practices for High-Risk Communications

Protecting sensitive communications requires enforcing full-disk device encryption, disabling automated cloud backups, utilizing short disappearing message timers, and hardening physical mobile endpoints.

talks.title: The Ghost of Internet Explorer in Windows
talks.teaser: Explores how legacy Internet Explorer components and MSHTML COM objects embedded in Windows continue to be weaponized for initial access and N-day exploitation.
talks.summary:
Legacy MSHTML Components in Modern Windows

Although Microsoft officially retired Internet Explorer, underlying legacy rendering engines (MSHTML / Trident) and associated COM interfaces remain deeply embedded within Windows for backward compatibility.

Weaponizing Internet Shortcuts and COM Objects

George Hughey and Rohit Mothe demonstrate how attackers craft malicious .URL and .LNK internet shortcut files that force modern Windows systems to render untrusted web content using deprecated, unpatched IE components.

Bypassing Mark-of-the-Web and Security Controls

Exploiting legacy URL protocol handlers bypasses Windows Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW) protections and application reputation filters, delivering zero-click and one-click remote code execution.

Remediation and Component Disablement

Defending enterprise environments requires disabling legacy IE protocol handlers via Group Policy, blocking unneeded COM class instantiation, and enforcing strict Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC).

talks.title: Turning Microsoft's Login Page into our Phishing Infrastructure
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how red teams can abuse legitimate Microsoft login branding parameters and OAuth endpoints to host convincing, high-trust phishing infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Abusing Trust in Enterprise Identity Portals

Users and automated email security filters are trained to trust authentic Microsoft login domains (such as login.microsoftonline.com) during enterprise single sign-on (SSO) workflows.

Manipulating Tenant Branding and OAuth Parameters

Keanu Nys reveals how attackers can abuse Microsoft Entra ID tenant branding features, customizable login pages, and OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoints to present highly customized phishing lures hosted entirely on legitimate Microsoft infrastructure.

Bypassing Modern Email Filters and Security Gateways

Because the underlying links point to valid Microsoft certificates and domains, automated Secure Email Gateways (SEGs) fail to classify the redirection links as malicious.

Defensive Detection and Conditional Access

Mitigating identity portal abuse requires enforcing FIDO2 phishing-resistant authentication, configuring strict Entra ID cross-tenant access restrictions, and monitoring abnormal OAuth consent grants.

talks.title: Making a Custom Hashcat Module to Solve a Decade-Old Puzzle Challenge
talks.teaser: Details the development of a high-performance custom OpenCL Hashcat kernel to crack non-standard cryptographic constructions in a decade-old puzzle challenge.
talks.summary:
Cracking Non-Standard Cryptographic Hashes

Standard password cracking utilities support hundreds of common hash types, but custom CTF challenges and legacy cryptographic algorithms often require specialized cracking logic.

Developing Custom OpenCL Hashcat Modules

Joseph Gabay walks through the technical process of writing optimized OpenCL and CUDA kernels for Hashcat to execute parallelized cryptographic operations on GPU hardware.

Optimizing GPU Register Usage and Parallelism

Achieving billions of candidate hashes per second requires tuning thread occupancy, minimizing branch divergence, and optimizing GPU shared memory lookups for non-standard cryptographic primitives.

Solving a Decade-Old Mystery Challenge

Deploying the customized Hashcat module successfully cracked the complex target hash, demonstrating high-performance GPU programming methodologies for cryptanalysis.

talks.title: Mastering Apple Endpoint Security for Advanced macOS Malware Detection
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle provides an advanced guide to Apple's Endpoint Security framework, demonstrating how to build robust, kernel-level telemetry and macOS malware detection.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of macOS Security Telemetry

Apple transitioned from deprecated Kernel Extensions (KEXTs) to the Endpoint Security (ES) framework, providing user-space security products with kernel-level event monitoring and authorization capabilities.

Mastering Endpoint Security Events and Handlers

Patrick Wardle breaks down the technical implementation of ES clients, detailing how to subscribe to process execution, file system modifications, IPC mach messaging, and dynamic dylib loading events.

Detecting Advanced macOS Malware Tradecraft

Leveraging granular ES telemetry enables defenders to detect stealthy macOS malware techniques, including synthetic click generation, Dylib hijacking, LaunchDaemon persistence, and TCC permission bypasses.

Building Open-Source Defensive Tools

Sharing open-source detection engineering methodologies equips macOS administrators and security researchers to develop robust, native endpoint monitoring solutions.

talks.title: Invoking Gemini Agents with a Google Calendar Invite
talks.teaser: Demonstrates an indirect prompt injection attack where a Google Calendar invite autonomously triggers Gemini AI agents to exfiltrate private user emails and files.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Autonomous AI Agents in Productivity Suites

Integrating AI agents (such as Google Gemini) into personal productivity tools allows automated parsing of emails, scheduling of calendar events, and retrieval of documents across cloud accounts.

Indirect Prompt Injection via Calendar Invites

Ben Nassi, Or Yair, and Stav Cohen demonstrate an indirect prompt injection attack where an adversary sends a seemingly normal Google Calendar invitation embedded with hidden adversarial instructions.

Autonomous Agent Hijacking and Data Exfiltration

When Gemini processes the user's daily schedule, the embedded payload overrides the agent's core instructions, autonomously querying private emails, searching Google Drive for sensitive documents, and exfiltrating data via web requests.

Architectural Guardrails for Connected AI Ecosystems

Mitigating autonomous agent exploitation requires establishing strict trust boundaries between untrusted external data and internal API execution, requiring user confirmation for high-privilege actions.

talks.title: The UnRightful Heir: My dMSA Is Your New Domain Admin
talks.teaser: Discloses critical design flaws in delegated Managed Service Accounts (dMSAs) in Windows Server 2025, enabling unprivileged domain users to become Domain Admins.
talks.summary:
Delegated Managed Service Accounts in Windows Server 2025

Microsoft introduced delegated Managed Service Accounts (dMSAs) to simplify service account management, automate Kerberos SPN provisioning, and enhance enterprise credential hygiene.

Discovering Architectural Privilege Escalation Flaws

Yuval Gordon reveals fundamental design flaws in dMSA delegation inheritance and Kerberos ticket-granting routines in Active Directory environments running Windows Server 2025.

From Standard Domain User to Domain Admin

By manipulating dMSA object properties and exploiting Kerberos constrained delegation misconfigurations, unprivileged domain users can impersonate delegated service identities and escalate to Domain Admin.

Hardening Active Directory Identity Infrastructure

Securing dMSA deployments requires applying Microsoft directory patches, auditing dMSA creation permissions, and enforcing strict delegation boundary policies across Active Directory domains.

talks.title: Infecting the Boot to Own the Kernel
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how boot-level vulnerabilities and flawed UEFI implementations bypass Secure Boot to execute persistent kernel-level bootkits.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Secure Boot

UEFI Secure Boot is designed to establish a cryptographic chain of trust from the hardware bootloader through the operating system kernel, blocking unsigned code execution.

Exploiting Vulnerabilities in UEFI Bootloaders

Alejandro Vazquez and Maria San Jose analyze implementation flaws in third-party signed UEFI binaries and bootloader components that allow attackers to bypass signature validation.

Installing Persistent Ring-0 Bootkits

Manipulating boot configuration parameters and exploiting memory corruption flaws during early boot allows attackers to patch kernel memory, disable Driver Signature Enforcement, and achieve persistent ring-0 execution.

Defensive Architecture and Firmware Revocation

Mitigating bootkits requires maintaining updated Secure Boot Forbidden Signature Databases (DBX), deploying Hardware Root of Trust, and enforcing firmware integrity monitoring.

talks.title: TSPU: Russia's Firewall and Defending Against Digital Repression
talks.teaser: Analyzes the technical architecture of Russia's TSPU deep packet inspection censorship firewall and presents novel evasion techniques for circumvention.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Sovereign Censorship Systems

Russia's Technical Means of Countering Threats (TSPU) represents a centralized deep packet inspection (DPI) censorship system deployed across domestic Internet Service Providers to block independent media and secure protocols.

Reverse Engineering TSPU Filtering Mechanics

Benjamin Mixon-Baca presents extensive empirical research analyzing how TSPU hardware parses SNI headers, inspects TLS handshakes, and executes active protocol throttling (such as Tor and WireGuard degradation).

Novel Evasion and Circumvention Primitives

Researchers demonstrate practical censorship circumvention techniques—including TCP packet fragmentation, SNI padding, and transport layer obfuscation—that bypass TSPU filtering.

Digital Rights and Circumvention Resilience

Understanding state censorship technology empowers digital rights organizations and software developers to engineer censorship-resistant communication tools for citizens living under digital repression.

talks.title: Unveiling the Perils of the TorchScript Engine in PyTorch
talks.teaser: Discloses multiple memory corruption and deserialization vulnerabilities in PyTorch's TorchScript JIT engine that allow arbitrary remote code execution via malicious AI models.
talks.summary:
PyTorch TorchScript and JIT Execution Engine

PyTorch TorchScript allows machine learning models to be serialized into standalone C++ runtimes for high-performance production inference across cloud servers and edge devices.

Analyzing the TorchScript Intermediate Representation

Ji'an Zhou and Lishuo Song audit the TorchScript JIT compiler, bytecode interpreter, and model deserialization routines, uncovering critical memory corruption and type confusion flaws.

Remote Code Execution via Weaponized Models

Crafting malicious model files targeting TorchScript parser vulnerabilities allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on cloud inference servers upon loading the model, bypassing Python sandbox restrictions.

Securing Machine Learning Model Pipelines

Remediating TorchScript vulnerabilities requires ML developers to treat untrusted model weights as untrusted binaries, enforce strict deserialization schemas, and run inference within isolated containers.

talks.title: Preventing One of The Largest Supply-Chain Attacks in History
talks.teaser: Provides an insider breakdown of detecting and neutralizing the historic XZ Utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094) before widespread Linux distribution deployment.
talks.summary:
The XZ Utils Supply-Chain Backdoor (CVE-2024-3094)

The XZ Utils compromise represents one of the most sophisticated multi-year open-source supply chain attacks in history, embedding a covert backdoor into upstream liblzma compression code.

Deconstructing the Multi-Stage Injection Mechanism

Maksim Shudrak provides a detailed technical breakdown of how the backdoor was concealed across obfuscated test files, injected during M4 build script execution, and hooked into OpenSSH authentication routines via IFUNC symbols.

Discovery, Reverse Engineering, and Neutralization

The talk chronicles the serendipitous discovery of anomalous CPU latency, rapid collaborative reverse engineering across the security community, and swift upstream neutralization before public releases reached stable Linux distributions.

Transforming Open-Source Supply Chain Security

Preventing future open-source supply chain compromises requires automated build artifact verification, reproducible builds, maintainer transparency, and enhanced funding for critical open-source infrastructure.

talks.title: Building the First Open Source Hackable Quantum Sensor
talks.teaser: Introduces the first open-source, low-cost hackable quantum sensor using Nitrogen-Vacancy centers in diamond to explore quantum sensing applications.
talks.summary:
Principles of Quantum Sensing and NV Centers

Quantum sensing utilizes the quantum mechanical properties of matter—such as Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in synthetic diamonds—to measure magnetic fields, temperature, and RF radiation with extreme precision.

Designing an Open-Source Quantum Sensing Platform

Mark Carney and Victoria Kumaran present an open-source hardware design that combines green laser excitation, microwave RF manipulation, and optical photodiode readouts into an accessible, low-cost sensor.

Hacking and Calibrating Quantum Measurements

Researchers demonstrate how to calibrate optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra and interface the sensor with microcontrollers to measure minute electromagnetic variations.

Democratizing Quantum Hardware Research

Releasing open hardware schematics and signal processing software enables makers, university researchers, and security practitioners to experiment with quantum sensing technology.

talks.title: Automated Unpacking & Deobfuscation of Nested VM-Based Protectors
talks.teaser: Presents a dynamic analysis framework for automatically unpacking and deobfuscating nested virtual-machine-based software protectors used in advanced malware.
talks.summary:
Virtual-Machine-Based Code Obfuscation

VM-based protectors (such as VMProtect and custom malware hypervisors) translate native CPU instructions into proprietary virtual bytecode executed by an embedded interpreter, confounding traditional static decompilers.

Challenges of Nested Virtualization

Advanced malware authors layer multiple virtual machines inside one another, creating nested interpreter loops that thwart manual reverse engineering and trace analysis.

Automated Symbolic Execution and De-Virtualization

Agostino Panico introduces an automated analysis framework utilizing dynamic binary instrumentation (DBI) and symbolic execution to trace VM execution loops, isolate bytecode handlers, and reconstruct native assembly.

Accelerating Malware Triage and Analysis

Automating the de-virtualization of nested VM protectors significantly reduces the time required for malware analysts and reverse engineers to analyze sophisticated threat payloads.

talks.title: DC101 Panel
talks.teaser: DEF CON veterans and village organizers provide newcomers with essential survival tips, track navigation strategies, and advice for navigating the conference.
talks.summary:
In this essential orientation panel from the DEF CON 33 Main Stage, veteran organizers and Goons—including Alethe Denis, Nikita Kronenberg, Zziks, and Nicole Schwartz—present "DC101," the definitive hacker survival guide for first-time attendees and returning veterans. Opening at 00:00, the panel introduces the sprawling scale of the convention and outlines strategies for navigating the event without burning out.

At 09:01, the speakers spotlight key conference accessibility and wellness spaces, highlighting the Chillout Room equipped with quiet seating, earplugs, and sensory toys designed to support neurodivergent attendees and offer respite from sensory overload. At 18:01, the panel reinforces the golden rules of convention health, famously reviewing the "3-2-1 rule"—requiring a minimum of three hours of sleep, two square meals, and one shower every day—while debunking the myth that liquid meal supplements are a substitute for proper nutrition and hydration.

The panel transitions to open Q&A at 27:00, advising attendees on using official scheduling apps, selecting village workshops, connecting with local DEF CON Groups, and building lifelong professional friendships across the global hacker community. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: SCCM: The Tree That Always Bears Bad Fruits
talks.teaser: Explores new offensive attack paths and privilege escalation techniques targeting Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (MECM/SCCM) in enterprise networks.
talks.summary:
SCCM as an Enterprise Management Engine

Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM / MECM) manages software deployment, operating system imaging, and patch compliance across thousands of enterprise endpoints with high administrative privileges.

Discovering New SCCM Attack Paths

Mehdi Elyassa demonstrates novel exploitation techniques targeting SCCM client enrollment, network access accounts, unencrypted PXE boot media, and site server database trusts.

Lateral Movement and Domain Dominance

Exploiting misconfigured administrative roles and abusing site control scripts allows attackers with low-privilege domain access to coerce credentials, deploy malicious client policies, and achieve full Domain Admin.

Hardening SCCM Architectures

Securing SCCM deployments requires eliminating Network Access Accounts, enforcing enhanced security for PXE environments, and auditing administrative role assignments across site hierarchies.

talks.title: Rebadged, Relabeled, Rooted: Pwnage via Solar Supply Chain
talks.teaser: Uncovers widespread firmware backdoors and hardware vulnerabilities in commercial solar inverters and energy management gateways across global supply chains.
talks.summary:
The Rapid Growth of Distributed Solar Infrastructure

Distributed solar generation and energy storage systems rely on smart solar inverters and cloud-connected telemetry gateways to balance power delivery to national electric grids.

Reverse Engineering Rebadged Solar Inverters

Anthony Rose and Jake Krasnov analyze dozens of commercial solar inverter models, discovering that many brands are simply rebadged white-label hardware containing identical firmware vulnerabilities.

Hardcoded Root Access and Unauthenticated APIs

Inspecting device firmware reveals hardcoded master credentials, insecure cloud management protocols, and unauthenticated local APIs that allow remote attackers to alter power output parameters and trip circuit breakers.

Securing Renewable Critical Infrastructure

Protecting renewable energy systems demands supply chain provenance auditing, independent hardware security testing, and strict network segmentation for smart energy gateways.

talks.title: Emulating Embedded Linux Devices at Scale w LightTouch Firmware Rehosting
talks.teaser: Introduces LightTouch, an automated firmware rehosting framework that enables scalable dynamic analysis and fuzzing of embedded Linux devices in QEMU.
talks.summary:
Challenges of Embedded Firmware Dynamic Analysis

Performing dynamic security analysis on embedded Linux firmware typically requires physical hardware or labor-intensive manual QEMU environment configuration.

LightTouch: Automated Firmware Rehosting

S Polke introduces LightTouch, a lightweight firmware rehosting framework that automatically extracts root filesystems, patches hardware dependencies, and boots embedded Linux firmware in emulated QEMU environments.

Fuzzing and Vulnerability Discovery at Scale

By virtualizing hardware peripherals and intercepting system calls, LightTouch enables automated dynamic analysis and large-scale fuzzing across diverse router, IP camera, and IoT firmware images.

Accelerating IoT Security Auditing

Automating firmware emulation empowers researchers to audit hundreds of embedded devices concurrently without acquiring physical hardware units.

talks.title: Bypassing Intent Destination Checks, LaunchAnyWhere Privilege Escalation
talks.teaser: Discloses new Intent redirection vulnerabilities in modern Android frameworks that bypass destination checks to achieve LaunchAnyWhere privilege escalation.
talks.summary:
Android Inter-Process Communication and Intents

Android applications and system services rely on Intents to pass data and invoke activities across application boundaries, governed by strict component permission checks.

Bypassing Intent Destination Checks

Qidan He reveals novel parser discrepancies and state inconsistencies in modern Android OS frameworks that allow unprivileged third-party apps to bypass destination validation on PendingIntents.

Executing LaunchAnyWhere Privilege Escalation

Exploiting these Intent redirection flaws enables attackers to launch arbitrary unexported system activities, execute privileged background operations, and achieve full device compromise.

Remediation in Android Platform Frameworks

Securing Android IPC requires operating system updates enforcing explicit Intent matching and strict component permission boundaries.

talks.title: Stories from a Tor Dev
talks.teaser: Tor Project co-founder Roger Dingledine shares operational war stories, censorship battles, and technical milestones from two decades of developing the Tor network.
talks.summary:
Two Decades of Onion Routing and Anonymity

The Tor network provides privacy, anonymity, and censorship circumvention for millions of users worldwide, including journalists, activists, and citizens living under repressive regimes.

Operational Battles Against State Censorship

Roger Dingledine recounts real-world encounters defending Tor against nationwide blocking efforts in Iran, Russia, and China, detailing the development of Pluggable Transports and bridge distribution systems.

Maintaining Network Health and Directory Consensus

Managing a distributed network of thousands of volunteer relay nodes requires continuous defense against malicious exit nodes, Sybil attacks, and directory consensus manipulation.

The Future of Online Privacy and Human Rights

Dingledine emphasizes the vital role of open-source privacy technologies in protecting human rights, privacy, and freedom of expression across the globe.

talks.title: Unmasking the Snitch Puck: IoT Surveillance Tech in the School Bathroom
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers commercial vape and sound monitoring sensors installed in school restrooms, uncovering unauthenticated telemetry feeds and cloud vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Environmental IoT Monitoring

Schools increasingly deploy connected sensor pucks in restrooms and private areas to monitor vaping, noise anomalies, and aggressive behavior, raising significant privacy and surveillance concerns.

Hardware Teardown and Sensor Extraction

Reynaldo and nyx tear down popular commercial sensor devices, reverse engineering their microcontrollers, microphone arrays, and optical smoke detection hardware.

Insecure Cloud Communication and Audio Leakage

Analyzing network traffic and firmware reveals unencrypted telemetry broadcasts, unauthenticated cloud API endpoints, and potential raw audio stream exposure over local Wi-Fi networks.

Ethical and Privacy Dimensions of Campus Surveillance

Evaluating school surveillance technology underscores the necessity of transparency, data minimization, and rigorous independent hardware security assessments in educational institutions.

talks.title: Mac PRT Cookie Theft & Entra ID Persistence
talks.teaser: Demonstrates techniques for stealing Microsoft Primary Refresh Tokens (PRT) and cookies on macOS endpoints to achieve persistent access to Entra ID cloud resources.
talks.summary:
Primary Refresh Tokens in macOS Enterprise Environments

Enterprises deploying Microsoft Entra ID with macOS endpoints rely on Primary Refresh Tokens (PRTs) stored inside system keychains and SSO extensions to provide seamless single sign-on across corporate SaaS apps.

Extracting PRT Cookies and SSO Secrets on macOS

Shang-De Jiang, Dong-Yi Ye, and Tung-lin Lee demonstrate how attackers with local user access can bypass macOS Keychain protections and extract active PRT session cookies from enterprise browser caches and Microsoft SSO plug-ins.

Persistent Cloud Access and Bypassing MFA

Replaying extracted PRT cookies allows adversaries to impersonate users across Azure, Office 365, and corporate cloud resources without triggering multi-factor authentication (MFA) or device compliance checks.

Defending Enterprise macOS Identity Endpoints

Hardening macOS identity infrastructure requires enforcing strict Keychain access controls, utilizing Secure Enclave hardware PRT binding, and deploying continuous conditional access evaluation in Entra ID.

talks.title: Finding and Exploiting Kernel Vulnerabilities in the eBPF Subsystem
talks.teaser: Examines vulnerability patterns in the Linux eBPF verifier and JIT compiler, demonstrating root privilege escalation via memory corruption.
talks.summary:
The eBPF Subsystem and In-Kernel Verification

Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) allows unprivileged and privileged user-space programs to execute sandboxed code inside the Linux kernel, relying on a complex in-kernel static verifier for memory safety.

Flaws in eBPF Verifier Range Tracking and ALU Logic

Agostino Panico analyzes subtle arithmetic logic errors, bounds-tracking mistakes, and 32-bit vs. 64-bit sign extension bugs within the eBPF verifier engine.

Bypassing Kernel Mitigations to Gain Root

By tricking the verifier into calculating incorrect register bounds, an attacker can construct out-of-bounds read/write primitives in kernel memory, defeating KASLR and escalating to full root privileges.

Hardening eBPF and Kernel Verifier Defenses

Securing the eBPF subsystem requires restricting unprivileged eBPF execution via sysctl, deploying automated kernel fuzzing, and integrating formal verification into verifier rule sets.

talks.title: HTTP/1.1 Must Die! The Desync Endgame
talks.teaser: James Kettle unleashes novel HTTP request smuggling and desync attack classes against modern web infrastructure, arguing for the retirement of HTTP/1.1.
talks.summary:
The Persistent Peril of HTTP/1.1 Framing

HTTP/1.1 request parsing relies on ambiguous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding header delimiters. Despite years of patch efforts, parsing discrepancies between front-end reverse proxies and backend servers continue to spawn critical request smuggling vulnerabilities.

New Desync Primitives and Parser Differentials

James Kettle presents the latest evolution of desync attacks, demonstrating novel techniques to bypass WAFs, poison web caches, and desynchronize connections across complex multi-tiered cloud architectures.

Weaponizing Request Smuggling in Production

Real-world case studies illustrate how subtle protocol desynchronization allows unauthenticated attackers to hijack user sessions, bypass authentication gateways, and steal sensitive credentials.

The Endgame: Moving Beyond HTTP/1.1

Kettle argues that fundamental protocol design flaws make HTTP/1.1 impossible to parse securely at scale, urging the web ecosystem to transition fully to binary, length-delimited protocols like HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

talks.title: Pre-Auth RCE, Arbitrary SMS & Adjacent Attacks on 5G and 4G_LTE Routers
talks.teaser: Discloses multiple pre-authentication remote code execution and arbitrary SMS vulnerabilities across popular consumer and industrial 4G/5G cellular routers.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Cellular Gateways

Commercial 4G LTE and 5G cellular routers provide primary and failover connectivity for industrial control networks, retail point-of-sale systems, and remote field deployments.

Pre-Authentication RCE and SMS Exploitation

Edward Warren details zero-day vulnerabilities in cellular router web management daemons and SMS parsing engines. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send crafted SMS messages or HTTP requests to trigger buffer overflows and achieve root shell access.

Adjacent Network Attacks and Cellular Pivoting

Once compromised, cellular gateways allow attackers to pivot across adjacent carrier subnets, intercept incoming multi-factor authentication SMS codes, and breach connected enterprise internal networks.

Hardening Cellular Router Deployments

Securing cellular endpoints requires disabling external WAN management interfaces, enforcing strong carrier APN isolation, and applying vendor firmware updates immediately.

talks.title: CTRAPS: CTAP Impersonation, API Confusion Attacks on FIDO2
talks.teaser: Presents CTRAPS, a novel class of API confusion and impersonation attacks targeting the Client to Authenticator Protocol (CTAP) in FIDO2 hardware keys.
talks.summary:
FIDO2 and CTAP Protocol Foundations

FIDO2 and WebAuthn rely on the Client to Authenticator Protocol (CTAP2) to facilitate secure, phishing-resistant public-key authentication between host platforms and hardware security keys over USB, NFC, and BLE.

CTRAPS: API Confusion and State Impersonation

M Casagrande and D Antonioli uncover structural flaws in CTAP protocol state machines and host operating system authenticator abstractions, introducing CTRAPS (Client-To-authenticator-Replay-And-Phishing-Suite).

Bypassing Origin Binding and Attestation

By manipulating API message sequences and exploiting cross-transport confusion between USB and virtual authenticators, adversaries can bypass origin-binding checks and trick users into authorizing unintended credentials.

Securing FIDO2 Implementations

Remediating CTRAPS requires browser vendors and the FIDO Alliance to enforce strict state machine validations, isolate virtual authenticator APIs, and update CTAP specifications.

talks.title: Client or Server? Hidden Sword of Damocles in Kafka
talks.teaser: Reveals critical architectural and deserialization vulnerabilities across Apache Kafka client and server implementations, enabling remote code execution.
talks.summary:
Apache Kafka in Modern Enterprise Architectures

Apache Kafka functions as the distributed event streaming backbone for thousands of enterprises, processing trillions of mission-critical messages across cloud pipelines daily.

Analyzing Kafka Client-Server Protocols

Ji'an Zhou, Ying Zhu, and ZiYang Li audit Kafka's network protocol implementations, SASL authentication handshakes, and third-party connector plugins, discovering critical security flaws.

Exploiting JNDI Injection and Deserialization in Connectors

Researchers demonstrate how untrusted data streams and malicious connector configurations trigger remote code execution via unsafe Java deserialization and JNDI injection on Kafka brokers and clients.

Hardening Kafka Streaming Deployments

Mitigating streaming vulnerabilities requires disabling dynamic plugin loading, enforcing strict SASL/SCRAM authentication, and deploying network segmentation around event streaming clusters.

talks.title: Siriously Leaky: Exploring Overlooked Attack Surfaces in Apple's Ecosystem
talks.teaser: Uncovers privacy vulnerabilities and local IPC leakage across Apple's Siri, CloudKit, and system daemon ecosystems on iOS and macOS.
talks.summary:
Inter-Process Communication in Apple's Ecosystem

Apple's macOS and iOS operating systems feature complex XPC services and system daemons managing user preferences, voice assistants, and cloud synchronization.

Auditing Siri and System Daemon IPC Endpoints

Richard Im investigates unvalidated XPC endpoints and entitlement checks across background services, discovering mechanisms that allow sandboxed applications to access private user telemetry.

Extracting User Data and Bypassing TCC

Exploiting improper IPC authorization allows third-party applications to query voice transcription histories, access location logs, and bypass Apple's Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) security framework.

Hardening macOS and iOS Entitlements

Securing Apple platforms requires strengthening XPC message validation, enforcing granular entitlement requirements, and auditing system daemon APIs for cross-application leakage.

talks.title: Passkeys Pwned: Turning WebAuthn Against Itself
talks.teaser: Demonstrates architectural and implementation weaknesses in commercial passkey syncing and WebAuthn relying party implementations.
talks.summary:
The Industry Push for Passwordless Passkeys

Passkeys and WebAuthn are widely adopted across consumer platforms to eliminate password-based attacks and provide phishing-resistant authentication.

Auditing Relying Party Implementations

S Pratap Singh, J Lin, and D Seetoh evaluate how major online services implement WebAuthn server-side verification, discovering widespread flaws in challenge-response validation and session binding.

Credential Takeover via Passkey Registration Flaws

Flaws in multi-factor recovery workflows and flawed fallback mechanisms allow attackers to register unauthorized passkeys onto victim accounts or abuse synchronization flaws in cloud passkey vaults.

Building Resilient Passkey Architectures

Enterprises deploying WebAuthn must enforce strict challenge validation, bind passkey sessions to verified client devices, and maintain secure account recovery fallbacks.

talks.title: China's 5+ Year Campaign to Penetrate Perimeter Network Defenses
talks.teaser: Sophos researcher Andrew Brandt chronicles a five-year investigation into Chinese nation-state campaigns weaponizing zero-days against perimeter firewall appliances.
talks.summary:
Nation-State Targeting of Perimeter Security Appliances

Chinese Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) groups have systematically targeted internet-exposed perimeter firewalls, VPN gateways, and edge routers to establish persistent footholds into enterprise networks.

Weaponizing Zero-Day Exploits Against Security Hardware

Andrew Brandt details the discovery and analysis of multiple zero-day remote code execution vulnerabilities exploited by state-sponsored actors against Sophos firewalls and enterprise gateway devices.

Sophisticated In-Memory Implants and Rootkits

Adversaries deployed bespoke Linux kernel rootkits and in-memory backdoors engineered to evade firmware integrity checks, disable logging, and survive device reboots.

Defensive Telemetry and Global Incident Response

Uncovering multi-year nation-state operations highlights the critical need for rapid automated hotpatching, continuous firmware threat hunting, and moving beyond perimeter-only defense models.

talks.title: Cyber Volunteering and Community Defense: 1 Year in DC Franklin
talks.teaser: Reflects on the first year of Project Franklin, exploring lessons learned in organizing cybersecurity volunteers to protect non-profits, local infrastructure, and communities.
talks.summary:
Grassroots Cybersecurity Defense for Underserved Sectors

Local municipalities, non-profit organizations, and community clinics face constant cyber threats from ransomware and extortion cartels, yet lack the financial resources to hire commercial security firms.

The Inception of Project Franklin

Organizers share the foundational journey of Project Franklin, establishing a coordinated network of volunteer cybersecurity professionals dedicated to providing pro-bono defense, incident response, and security auditing.

Operational Lessons and Practical Challenges

Overcoming legal liability hurdles, establishing vetted triage playbooks, and managing volunteer burnout represent critical operational milestones in scaling community cyber defense initiatives.

A Blueprint for Scalable Community Resilience

Project Franklin provides a replicable framework for cybersecurity communities worldwide to organize collective defense and safeguard critical local institutions.

talks.title: Cash, Drugs, and Guns: Why Your Safes Aren't Safe
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers electronic gun safes and commercial digital vaults, demonstrating effortless physical and electromagnetic bypasses across leading brands.
talks.summary:
Trust in Electronic and Biometric Safes

Consumers rely on electronic gun safes and smart security vaults to securely store firearms, narcotics, cash, and sensitive documents, trusting vendor claims of impenetrable digital security.

Reverse Engineering Digital Lock Controllers

Mark Omo and James Rowley analyze microcontrollers, solenoids, and electronic keypads across leading commercial safe manufacturers, uncovering severe design and firmware vulnerabilities.

Physical, EMP, and Logic Bypasses

Researchers demonstrate multiple zero-trace bypasses, including manipulating unshielded solenoid wiring, executing electromagnetic pulse (EMP) resets, and exploiting unauthenticated debug pins on exterior keypads.

Standards and Engineering for Physical Security

Fixing flawed electronic safe locks requires manufacturers to adopt hardened mechanical backup locks, shielded solenoid enclosures, and cryptographically verified keypad buses.

talks.title: Exploiting Security Side Channels in E2E Encrypted Messengers
talks.teaser: Discloses network and timing side channels in end-to-end encrypted messaging apps that allow adversaries to reconstruct contact graphs and user activity.
talks.summary:
End-to-End Encryption and Residual Metadata

Modern messaging apps (such as Signal, WhatsApp, and Telegram) use robust end-to-end encryption to protect message contents. However, network-level and application-level side channels frequently leak metadata.

Analyzing Network Traffic and Typing Notifications

G Gegenheuber and M Gunther analyze packet timing, size distributions, and ephemeral feature handshakes (such as typing indicators and read receipts) across popular encrypted messengers.

Reconstructing User Contact Graphs and Activity

By monitoring passive network flows or sending probe packets, an adversary can determine when specific users are communicating, infer recipient identities, and reconstruct detailed social graphs without breaking cryptographic ciphers.

Mitigation Strategies for Encrypted Protocols

Eliminating metadata leakage requires implementing constant-rate packet padding, decoupling typing notifications from network broadcasts, and routing telemetry through mixnets.

talks.title: Not Just a Pipeline Leak: Reconstructing Real Attack Behind tj-actions
talks.teaser: Reconstructs the multi-stage CI/CD supply chain compromise of the popular tj-actions GitHub Action, detailing secret exfiltration and attacker tradecraft.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of CI/CD Pipelines

Modern software development relies on GitHub Actions and automated CI/CD workflows, where third-party actions execute with access to repository secrets, cloud credentials, and release tokens.

Reconstructing the tj-actions Compromise

Aviad Hahami provides a detailed forensic reconstruction of the real-world supply chain attack targeting the widely used tj-actions/changed-files action.

Secret Harvesting and Malicious Pull Request Injection

Adversaries weaponized subtle pull request workflow triggers and repository permissions to inject malicious payloads, exfiltrating GitHub tokens and AWS credentials from thousands of downstream organizations.

Hardening Enterprise CI/CD Pipelines

Protecting build infrastructure requires pinning actions to immutable commit SHAs, enforcing least-privilege token permissions, and monitoring runner execution logs for unauthorized outbound connections.

talks.title: Remote Code Execution via MIDI Messages
talks.teaser: Demonstrates remote code execution across audio software and operating system synthesis engines by weaponizing malformed MIDI protocol messages.
talks.summary:
The MIDI Protocol and Audio Software Stacks

The Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) protocol has governed electronic musical instruments and computer audio synthesis for four decades, operating as a trusted, real-time message stream.

Auditing MIDI Parsers and Sound Synthesis Daemons

Anna Antonenko investigates how modern operating systems, digital audio workstations (DAWs), and web browsers parse complex MIDI SysEx and control change packets.

Heap Corruption and Remote Exploitation

Malformed MIDI streams trigger buffer overflows and heap memory corruption in audio parsing libraries. Crafting malicious MIDI files or WebMIDI browser events enables arbitrary code execution on host systems.

Securing Legacy Media Protocol Parsers

Remediating MIDI exploitation requires developers to rewrite legacy C/C++ audio parsing engines in memory-safe languages and enforce strict input length boundaries on all SysEx message handlers.

talks.title: Kill Chain Reloaded: Abuse Legacy Paths for Stealth Persistence
talks.teaser: Uncovers overlooked legacy Windows execution paths and registry mechanisms to establish stealthy persistence that evades modern EDR detection.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Endpoint Persistence

Modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents rigorously monitor common persistence vectors, such as standard Run keys, scheduled tasks, and Windows services.

Rediscovering Obscure Legacy Execution Paths

A Hernando and B Martinez delve into decades of Windows architecture, identifying overlooked registry subkeys, legacy COM handler redirections, and deprecated shell extension paths that bypass EDR heuristics.

Achieving Stealthy, Unmonitored Persistence

By leveraging legitimate operating system binaries and dormant subsystem configurations, red teams can maintain durable persistence across system reboots without generating suspicious process telemetry.

Detection Engineering and Registry Auditing

Blue teams can enhance visibility by expanding behavioral registry monitoring rules, auditing dormant COM registrations, and conducting regular baseline comparisons of endpoint configuration states.

talks.title: Conjuring Hardware Failures for Cross-Ring Privilege Escalation
talks.teaser: Christopher Domas demonstrates how software-controlled microarchitectural stresses induce transient hardware faults to achieve cross-ring privilege escalation.
talks.summary:
Pushing Silicon Beyond Specification Limits

Modern x86 microprocessors operate under complex power delivery, thermal management, and clock distribution constraints governed by integrated microcode and firmware.

Software-Induced Microarchitectural Stress

Christopher Domas demonstrates how unprivileged software can execute precise, high-density instruction patterns that generate extreme current draw and localized voltage drops within CPU execution units.

Triggering Predictable Silicon Faults

Inducing transient hardware brownouts causes targeted CPU instruction decoders and privilege check registers to glitch, allowing unprivileged user-space code to break out into kernel and hypervisor execution rings.

Implications for Microprocessor Security Architecture

This research challenges the boundary between hardware and software security, demonstrating that software can directly subvert silicon physical guarantees without specialized physical hardware testbeds.

talks.title: Escaping the Privacy Sandbox with Client-Side Deanonymization Attacks
talks.teaser: Eugene Lim demonstrates novel client-side attacks that subvert Google's Privacy Sandbox APIs to deanonymize users and track web browsing histories.
talks.summary:
