The Architecture of Google's Privacy Sandbox

Google developed the Privacy Sandbox framework to replace third-party cookies with privacy-preserving APIs (such as Topics, Protected Audience, and Attribution Reporting) designed to support digital advertising without cross-site tracking.

Discovering Information Leaks in Sandbox APIs

Eugene Lim presents a series of novel client-side exploit techniques that chain subtle timing discrepancies, storage side channels, and API state leaks within the Privacy Sandbox implementation.

Cross-Site Tracking and User Deanonymization

By manipulating API query parameters across collaborating domains, an adversary can bypass intentional differential privacy noise, reconstructing individual browsing histories and linking anonymous sessions to real-world identities.

Securing Privacy-Preserving Web Standards

Preventing deanonymization attacks requires browser vendors to mathematically prove noise bounds, enforce strict cross-origin partitioning, and eliminate synchronous side-channel oracles.

talks.title: So Long, and Thanks for All the Phish
talks.teaser: Analyzes the evolution of enterprise phishing defense and demonstrates novel reverse-proxy adversary-in-the-middle tradecraft to bypass modern authentication.
talks.summary:
The Arms Race in Enterprise Phishing

As organizations deploy automated email filtering, domain reputation checks, and multi-factor authentication, phishing operators continuously adapt their delivery mechanisms and credential harvesting infrastructure.

Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Tradecraft

Harrison Sand and Erlend Leiknes demonstrate advanced AiTM proxy architectures that capture live session cookies and authentication tokens in real time, bypassing traditional SMS and app-based MFA.

Evasion of Modern Email Defense Platforms

Techniques for leveraging legitimate SaaS platforms, CAPTCHA obfuscation, and dynamic user-agent fingerprinting allow phishing kits to evade automated security sandbox analysis.

Implementing Phishing-Resistant Authentication

Effectively countering modern AiTM phishing attacks requires organizations to transition to FIDO2 WebAuthn passkeys, enforce device attestation, and deploy conditional access policies.

talks.title: You Snooze You Lose: RPC Racer Winning RPC Endpoints Against Services
talks.teaser: Introduces RPC Racer, a technique that exploits race conditions in Windows RPC endpoint registration to hijack privileged system service communication.
talks.summary:
Windows Remote Procedure Call Architecture

Windows relies on Remote Procedure Call (RPC) interfaces for inter-process communication between user applications and privileged background services (such as LSASS, Spooler, and DCOM).

Race Conditions in RPC Endpoint Binding

Ron Ben Yizhak identifies a widespread timing flaw in how Windows system services register and bind dynamic RPC endpoints during system boot and service restarts.

RPC Racer: Hijacking Privileged Service Endpoints

The author introduces RPC Racer, an exploit technique that wins registration race conditions against legitimate services, allowing an unprivileged attacker to bind to intended service interfaces and intercept or manipulate privileged IPC messages.

Remediation and Defensive Guidance

Securing Windows RPC interfaces requires developers and Microsoft to enforce exclusive interface binding flags, mandate interface security callbacks, and audit endpoint registration timing.

talks.title: Inside Look at a Chinese Operational Relay Network
talks.teaser: Provides an inside look at a massive operational relay network (ORB) of compromised IoT devices and routers used by Chinese APT actors to obfuscate cyber attacks.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Operational Relay Networks (ORBs)

State-sponsored threat actors increasingly abandon fixed commercial VPNs in favor of dynamic Operational Relay Networks (ORBs) constructed from thousands of compromised small office/home office (SOHO) routers and IoT devices.

Architecture and Node Management

Michael Torres and Zane Hoffman analyze the technical architecture of a prominent Chinese APT relay network, detailing how compromised devices are chained together via custom proxy daemons to route operational traffic.

Tracking and Mapping Nation-State Traffic

By analyzing routing behaviors, node churn rates, and communication protocols, threat intelligence researchers successfully mapped the proxy mesh back to state-sponsored offensive campaigns.

Disrupting and Mitigating ORB Infrastructure

Mitigating the threat of operational relay networks requires global cooperation among router manufacturers, ISPs, and law enforcement to remediate edge device vulnerabilities and conduct coordinated infrastructure takedowns.

talks.title: Man in the Malware: Intercepting Adversarial Communications
talks.teaser: Demonstrates methodologies for intercepting and decrypting command-and-control traffic between active malware implants and adversary servers.
talks.summary:
The Challenge of Command-and-Control Visibility

Advanced malware families protect their command-and-control (C2) channels using custom symmetric encryption, dynamic domain generation algorithms (DGAs), and layered TLS tunnels.

Reverse Engineering Malware Cryptographic Protocols

Ben Folland walks through the technical process of extracting hardcoded cryptographic keys, decrypting config blocks, and reconstructing proprietary C2 communication protocols.

Man-in-the-Middle Interception and Emulation

By creating protocol-accurate server emulators and intercepting active C2 sessions, researchers can monitor adversary commands, track infected victim populations, and harvest operational threat intelligence.

Operationalizing Adversary Telemetry

Leveraging intercepted adversary communications enables defenders to generate proactive detection rules, alert compromised victims, and assist law enforcement in disrupting cybercrime syndicates.

talks.title: Kill List: Hacking an Assassination Site on the Dark Web
talks.teaser: Investigates the technical operation and server breach of a notorious darknet murder-for-hire scam site, exposing operations that led to real-world threat alerts.
talks.summary:
The Dark Web Murder-for-Hire Phenomenon

Underground darknet sites claiming to offer contract assassination services are almost universally financial extortion scams designed to steal Bitcoin from desperate users.

Breaching and Analyzing the Assassination Portal

Journalist Carl Miller and security researcher Chris Monteiro detail the technical breach and backend database extraction of the infamous 'Besa Mafia' and successor murder-for-hire websites.

Data Forensics and Threat-to-Life Triaging

Analyzing unencrypted message databases, order forms, and Bitcoin transaction logs uncovered hundreds of real-world kill orders, requiring urgent coordination with international law enforcement to warn potential victims.

Investigative Methodologies in Cybercrime Research

This investigation illustrates the complex ethical, technical, and legal challenges involved in researching dark web cybercrime and handling imminent threats to human life.

talks.title: Escaping the Privacy Sandbox with Client Side Deanonymization Attacks
talks.teaser: Eugene Lim demonstrates client-side exploit chains against Google's Privacy Sandbox APIs to defeat differential privacy noise and track web users.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Google's Privacy Sandbox

Google developed the Privacy Sandbox framework to replace third-party cookies with privacy-preserving APIs (such as Topics, Protected Audience, and Attribution Reporting) designed to support digital advertising without cross-site tracking.

Discovering Information Leaks in Sandbox APIs

Eugene Lim presents a series of novel client-side exploit techniques that chain subtle timing discrepancies, storage side channels, and API state leaks within the Privacy Sandbox implementation.

Cross-Site Tracking and User Deanonymization

Securing Privacy-Preserving Web Standards

Preventing deanonymization attacks requires browser vendors to mathematically prove noise bounds, enforce strict cross-origin partitioning, and eliminate synchronous side-channel oracles.

talks.title: Investigating Threat Actor Targeting Researchers, Academics
talks.teaser: Examines campaigns by nation-state actors (such as Iranian and DPRK groups) targeting cybersecurity researchers and think tanks via social engineering.
talks.summary:
Adversary Targeting of the Cybersecurity Community

Nation-state threat actors increasingly target vulnerability researchers, academic scholars, and foreign policy think tanks to acquire exploit tradecraft, intelligence reports, and access credentials.

Persona Construction and Social Engineering Tradecraft

C Tafani-Dereeper and M Muir analyze the sophisticated multi-platform personas utilized by Iranian (e.g., Charming Kitten) and North Korean (e.g., Lazarus) actors across LinkedIn, Twitter/X, and WhatsApp.

Custom Malware Delivery and Collaborative Lures

Adversaries establish rapport over weeks before delivering malicious collaboration invitations, trojanized IDA Pro plugins, or weaponized research papers containing custom backdoors.

Protecting the Research Community

Defending security researchers requires cultivating heightened operational awareness, validating collaborative identities through out-of-band channels, and sandboxing untrusted research tools.

talks.title: How a Vuln in Dealer Software Could've Unlocked Your Car
talks.teaser: Reveals critical API authorization vulnerabilities in automotive dealer management systems that allowed national admin account creation and remote vehicle control.
talks.summary:
Centralized Dealer Management Platforms

Automotive dealerships across the United States rely on centralized software platforms to manage inventory, service appointments, customer records, and connected vehicle features.

Discovering Broken Object Level Authorization Flaws

Eaton Zveare and R Piyush identified fundamental access control vulnerabilities in a leading automaker's dealer platform APIs. Unauthenticated parameter tampering allowed researchers to elevate privileges and create national administrative accounts.

Remote Vehicle Telematics Compromise

With national administrator access, researchers could query customer profiles, retrieve vehicle identification numbers (VINs), and transmit remote commands to lock, unlock, start, and track thousands of customer vehicles nationwide.

Lessons for Connected Automotive Ecosystems

Securing automotive dealer management portals demands strict API authentication, multi-factor authorization on administrative endpoints, and rigorous architectural reviews of third-party vendor platforms.

talks.title: Welcome to DEF CON 33
talks.teaser: DEF CON founder The Dark Tangent opens DEF CON 33, welcoming the hacker community, celebrating hacker culture, and setting the conference theme.
talks.summary:
DEF CON founder Jeff Moss ("The Dark Tangent") opens DEF CON 33 on the Main Stage, welcoming attendees and reflecting on the foundational ethos that has guided the conference since its inception [00:07, 03:47]. Moss outlines his golden rule for conference participants: spending half of their time immersing themselves in hands-on hacking and breaking technical systems, and the other half building social relationships and community connections [07:17].

Moss traces the evolution of DEF CON traditions, recounting how Capture the Flag (CTF) grew from informal, adversarial network skirmishes into the world's preeminent international cybersecurity tournament [11:04, 14:31]. He highlights how fringe curiosities explored by independent hackers consistently foreshadow the critical security priorities of global enterprises and nation-states years down the line, encouraging both first-timers and veteran hackers to dive into the challenges and culture of DEF CON 33 [17:54, 21:37].

talks.title: Voice Cloning Air Traffic Control: Vulnerabilities at Runway Crossings
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how real-time AI voice cloning and software-defined radios can inject fraudulent air traffic control clearances on unencrypted VHF frequencies.
talks.summary:
Unencrypted VHF Aviation Communications

Civil aviation relies almost entirely on analog, unencrypted Very High Frequency (VHF) amplitude modulation (AM) radio channels for air traffic control (ATC) voice clearances between towers and pilots.

AI Voice Cloning and Real-Time Synthesis

Andrew Logan demonstrates how neural voice cloning models trained on publicly available LiveATC feeds can replicate specific air traffic controller voices in near-real time.

Over-the-Air Transmission and Runway Hazard Scenarios

Transmitting cloned voice commands using software-defined radios (SDRs) creates severe safety hazards, including spoofing takeoff clearances or runway crossing authorizations in low-visibility conditions.

Mitigations and Future Aviation Protocols

Protecting air traffic communications requires transitioning to authenticated digital datalinks (such as CPDLC) and implementing voice watermarking and spatial RF transmitter verification.

talks.title: Virtualization Based Insecurity: Weaponizing VBS Enclaves
talks.teaser: Exposes architectural security flaws in Windows Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) enclaves, demonstrating how attackers weaponize isolated trust levels.
talks.summary:
Windows Virtualization-Based Security (VBS)

Microsoft VBS leverages hypervisor hardware virtualization to partition memory into isolated Virtual Trust Levels (VTLs), protecting sensitive security services (such as Credential Guard and isolated enclaves) from compromised operating system kernels.

Auditing VBS Enclave Communication Interfaces

Ori David analyzes the inter-VTL communication interfaces, hypercalls, and shared memory buffers connecting the standard Windows kernel (VTL 0) to secure enclaves (VTL 1).

Weaponizing Enclaves for Stealth and Evasion

Exploiting boundary synchronization bugs and shared memory pointer validation flaws allows attackers to manipulate enclave execution, bypass hypervisor isolation, and execute stealthy persistence mechanisms outside kernel visibility.

Hardening Hypervisor Trust Boundaries

Securing VBS environments requires Microsoft to enforce strict memory bounds checking across all VTL transition interfaces and continuously audit hypervisor trap handlers.

talks.title: Where’s My Crypto, Dude? The Ultimate Guide to Crypto Money Laundering
talks.teaser: Thomas Roccia breaks down the laundering pipelines used by cybercrime syndicates and ransomware groups across crypto mixers, bridges, and instant exchangers.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Cryptocurrency Laundering

Cybercrime cartels, ransomware operators, and state-sponsored groups generate billions in illicit cryptocurrency, necessitating sophisticated laundering pipelines to convert stolen tokens into clean fiat currency.

Deconstructing Modern Laundering Pipelines

Thomas Roccia analyzes the multi-stage laundering workflow, detailing the technical operation of coin mixers, decentralized cross-chain bridges, non-compliant instant swap services, and peer-to-peer cash brokers.

Tracing Illicit Flows Across Complex Blockchains

Using on-chain blockchain forensic methodologies and graph analysis, investigators track complex peeling chains, transaction hopping across EVM and non-EVM chains, and mixer exits.

Empowering Threat Intelligence and Asset Recovery

Understanding modern crypto laundering tradecraft enables threat analysts and law enforcement agencies to correlate disparate criminal campaigns and freeze illicit funds before cash-out.

talks.title: Breaking into Thousands of Cloud-Based VPNs with One Bug
talks.teaser: Discloses a critical vulnerability in cloud-managed enterprise VPN platforms that allowed unauthenticated administrative takeover across thousands of corporate networks.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Cloud-Managed Enterprise VPNs

Enterprises increasingly deploy cloud-managed VPN solutions to facilitate secure remote access for distributed workforces, relying on centralized SaaS dashboards for user provisioning and device policy enforcement.

Discovering Centralized Authentication Bypasses

David Cash and Rich Warren identify a critical architectural flaw in the cloud management control plane, where flawed SAML/OAuth session validation allowed unauthenticated attackers to elevate privileges to global tenant administrators.

National Tenant Compromise and Internal Network Pivoting

With global administrative access, researchers could manipulate client configuration profiles, deploy malicious routing rules, and gain unrestricted network access into thousands of corporate enterprise networks worldwide.

Hardening Cloud-Managed Network Infrastructure

Securing cloud VPN infrastructure requires enforcing strict tenant data isolation, conducting continuous cryptographic token validation, and mandating multi-party authorization for administrative configuration changes.

talks.title: Rusty Pearls: Postgres RCE on Cloud Databases
talks.teaser: Demonstrates remote code execution on managed cloud PostgreSQL databases by exploiting memory safety vulnerabilities in untrusted procedural language extensions.
talks.summary:
Managed Cloud Database Sandboxes

Cloud service providers (such as AWS, GCP, and Azure) offer managed PostgreSQL database instances, relying on restricted user roles and system sandboxes to prevent customers from executing code on the underlying host OS.

Auditing Procedural Languages and Rust Extensions

Tal Peleg and Coby Abrams audit procedural language runtimes (such as PL/Rust) and custom PostgreSQL extensions used to execute performant code inside database engines.

Memory Corruption to Host Remote Code Execution

Subtle memory safety bugs and compiler optimization oversights in extension loaders allow attackers to escape the PostgreSQL sandbox, executing arbitrary native code with host operating system privileges.

Securing Cloud Database Services

Remediating database RCE vectors requires cloud providers to run database processes in microVM-isolated environments (like Firecracker) and enforce strict capability dropping on all extension runtimes.

talks.title: How to Fake a Badge Like a Pro: Counterfeiting Event Credentials
talks.teaser: Details physical red team tradecraft for analyzing, cloning, and counterfeiting event security badges, holograms, and laminated credentials.
talks.summary:
The Role of Badges in Physical Security

Conferences, corporate offices, and secure facilities rely heavily on visual badges, RFID credentials, and holographic passes to grant physical access to sensitive zones.

Reverse Engineering Visual and Electronic Credentials

Russell Phillips breaks down the physical anatomy of security credentials, detailing techniques for analyzing laminate layers, holographic security foils, microprinting, and UV reactive inks.

Practical Counterfeiting Tools and Techniques

Using accessible desktop printing, thermal laminators, and RFID cloner tools, physical penetration testers can manufacture authentic-looking credentials capable of bypassing visual guard inspections.

Defensive Verification and Access Control Engineering

Mitigating credential counterfeiting requires facilities to deploy two-factor electronic verification, combine physical inspections with real-time biometric checks, and train security staff on badge forensic features.

talks.title: From Shanghai to the Shore: Threats in Global Shipping
talks.teaser: Examines cyber and physical attack surfaces across global maritime logistics, cargo container cranes, and automated port terminals.
talks.summary:
The Fragility of Global Maritime Logistics

Global trade depends on interconnected shipping networks, where automated port container terminals, customs clearing systems, and cargo ships form an indispensable supply chain.

Attack Surfaces in Port Automation and Shipboard OT

K Miltenberger and N Fredericksen examine vulnerabilities across Automated Stacking Cranes (ASCs), terminal operating systems (TOS), and vessel management networks.

Threat Scenarios and Cascading Economic Impact

Targeted cyber intrusions disrupting port logistics or falsifying cargo manifests can create massive supply chain gridlocks, paralyzing regional commerce and critical goods distribution.

Hardening Maritime Critical Infrastructure

Strengthening maritime cybersecurity requires establishing international OT security standards, conducting continuous port network monitoring, and implementing manual failover procedures.

talks.title: Making the DEF CON 33 Badge
talks.teaser: Mar details the design, engineering, artistic creation, and electronic manufacturing process behind the official DEF CON 33 electronic badge.
talks.summary:
The Tradition of the DEF CON Electronic Badge

The annual DEF CON badge represents a fusion of embedded engineering, artistic design, and interactive hacking challenges for tens of thousands of conference attendees.

Hardware Engineering and Component Selection

Badge creator Mar walks through the iterative hardware design process, from microcontroller and sensor selection to circuit schematic layout and power optimization.

Manufacturing and Production at Scale

Managing mass electronic manufacturing under strict deadlines requires solving PCB fabrication bottlenecks, automated surface-mount assembly challenges, and firmware flashing logistics.

Interactive Puzzles and Community Hacking

The finished badge features interactive hardware puzzles and expansion headers, encouraging attendees to reverse engineer the device and develop custom hardware add-ons.

talks.title: OverLAPS: Overriding LAPS Logic
talks.teaser: Discloses subtle logic and authorization bypasses in Microsoft Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) that enable credential theft.
talks.summary:
Windows LAPS in Enterprise Active Directory

Microsoft Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) manages and randomizes local administrator account passwords on domain-joined machines, storing credentials securely in Active Directory or Azure.

Discovering Logic and Authorization Flaws

Antoine Goichot analyzes the internal encryption and permission check mechanisms of Windows LAPS (including modern Azure-backed Windows LAPS), discovering subtle authorization discrepancies in password retrieval.

Overriding LAPS Logic for Lateral Movement

By manipulating object ACLs and exploiting attribute synchronization timing, attackers with delegated permissions can force password recalculation or access plaintext administrative passwords across domain endpoints.

Hardening LAPS Deployments

Securing LAPS requires implementing strict Active Directory attribute access controls, auditing password read events, and migrating to modern cloud-managed LAPS with end-to-end encryption.

talks.title: Turning Camera Surveillance on its Axis
talks.teaser: Demonstrates remote code execution and edge compromise across Axis enterprise IP cameras, turning surveillance devices into offensive pivot points.
talks.summary:
Enterprise IP Cameras as Perimeter Targets

Commercial IP surveillance cameras (such as Axis devices) are widely deployed across enterprise perimeters, critical infrastructure facilities, and government campuses, operating on privileged internal subnets.

Auditing Axis Camera Firmware and Daemons

Noam Moshe investigates the firmware architecture of Axis IP cameras, auditing proprietary video streaming daemons, VAPIX web APIs, and embedded ONVIF protocol services.

Unauthenticated Memory Corruption to Root Execution

Discovering critical buffer overflow and format string vulnerabilities allows unauthenticated network attackers to achieve arbitrary root code execution on camera endpoints.

Turning Cameras into Lateral Pivots

Compromised cameras allow attackers to manipulate video feeds, intercept physical access logs, and pivot deeper into segmented corporate and operational technology networks.

Remediation and Camera Network Segmentation

Securing enterprise surveillance systems requires applying vendor firmware patches, isolating camera devices onto dedicated VLANs, and disabling unnecessary cloud proxy features.

talks.title: Silent Leaks: Harvesting Secrets from Shared Linux Environments
talks.teaser: Explores techniques for harvesting cached credentials, environment tokens, and process memory artifacts across multi-tenant shared Linux systems.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Multi-User Linux Systems

Shared Linux servers, high-performance computing clusters, and container hosts often host multiple users and background processes with varying privilege levels.

Harvesting Secrets from Ephemeral Artifacts

Cernica Ionut Cosmin details stealthy techniques for recovering sensitive secrets from /proc filesystem pseudo-files, unlinked file descriptors, systemd service environments, and shared memory segments (/dev/shm).

Process Memory Dumping and Privilege Escalation

Unprivileged local users can monitor process execution timing, inspect inter-process communication pipes, and extract authentication tokens used by adjacent administrative processes.

Hardening Multi-User Linux Environments

Mitigating local secret leakage requires mounting /proc with hidepid=2, restricting ptrace permissions via Yama LSM, and adopting dedicated secret management services instead of shell environment variables.

talks.title: Hacking OBD II Emissions Testing
talks.teaser: Explores the evolution of vehicular emissions inspections from physical tailpipe sniffers to OBD-II queries and demonstrates how testing logic can be bypassed.
talks.summary:
Hardware Hacking and Physical Security

This talk covers hardware hacking techniques and physical security analysis. Topics include circuit board analysis, side-channel attacks, firmware extraction, and low-level debugging of hardware systems.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: The Ultimate Hack: Applying Lessons Learned from the Loss of TITAN
talks.teaser: US Coast Guard Rear Admiral John Mauger discusses safety culture, engineering integrity, and lessons learned from the investigation into the catastrophic loss of the TITAN submersible.
talks.summary:
Engineering Integrity and the TITAN Disaster

The catastrophic implosion of the OceanGate TITAN submersible in 2023 underscored the critical importance of rigorous engineering standards, independent certification, and transparent safety culture in extreme environments.

Investigative Findings from the Coast Guard Marine Board

Rear Admiral John Mauger reviews key operational and structural findings from the formal US Coast Guard investigation, analyzing how non-standard composite materials and bypassed certification protocols led to catastrophic structural failure.

The Hacker Mindset vs. Safety Engineering

While innovation and breaking established boundaries drive technological breakthroughs, high-consequence cyber-physical systems demand rigorous testing, fail-safe redundancy, and respect for physical laws.

Lessons for Technology and Cybersecurity Governance

The lessons of the TITAN disaster highlight the necessity of robust regulatory oversight, independent third-party validation, and continuous risk assessment across emerging technologies.

talks.title: Shaking Out Shells with SSHamble
talks.teaser: Metasploit creator HD Moore introduces SSHamble, a state-machine-driven scanning and analysis tool to uncover obscure implementation flaws across SSH servers.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity and Complexity of the SSH Protocol

Secure Shell (SSH) is the standard protocol for secure remote administration across millions of enterprise servers, network switches, and embedded devices worldwide.

SSHamble: State-Machine-Driven Protocol Auditing

HD Moore introduces SSHamble, an open-source security scanner that maps and analyzes SSH server state machines, banner discrepancies, and protocol negotiation handshakes at Internet scale.

Uncovering Implementation Flaws and Authentication Bypasses

By systematically probing non-standard packet sequences and cipher combinations, SSHamble identifies misconfigured authentication modules, memory leaks, and obscure pre-authentication vulnerabilities in proprietary SSH daemons.

Actionable Reconnaissance for Defenders and Researchers

Deploying automated SSH state-machine analysis enables organizations to audit their external attack surface, identify deprecated cryptographic algorithms, and enforce strict SSH hardening standards.

talks.title: Paywall Optional: Stream for Free w/ New Technique, RRE
talks.teaser: Introduces Real-time Re-encryption (RRE), a technique that defeats commercial DRM and streaming paywalls across digital media platforms.
talks.summary:
Digital Rights Management in Video Streaming

Commercial streaming platforms rely on Digital Rights Management (DRM) technologies (such as Widevine and FairPlay) to encrypt media streams and enforce subscriber paywalls.

Real-Time Re-Encryption (RRE) Mechanics

Farzan Karim presents Real-time Re-encryption (RRE), a novel methodology that intercepts decrypted media buffers from trusted hardware decoders and re-encrypts streams with user-controlled keys in real time.

Defeating Browser and Hardware DRM Protections

By exploiting memory mapping flaws and API timing discrepancies within browser media pipelines, RRE extracts pristine video and audio streams without triggering anti-piracy protections.

Hardening Media Delivery Architectures

Securing streaming media platforms requires continuous hardware attestation, server-side watermarking, and dynamic DRM key rotation.

talks.title: Mind the Data Voids: Hijacking Copilot Trust
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how adversaries exploit data voids in LLM training corpora and search indexes to manipulate Microsoft Copilot answers and inject untrusted content.
talks.summary:
Data Voids in Large Language Model Retrieval

Generative AI assistants (such as Microsoft Copilot) rely on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to supplement model knowledge with real-time web search results and corporate indexes.

Weaponizing Data Voids and Knowledge Gaps

Tobias Diehl explains how attackers identify 'data voids'—obscure search queries or emerging topics with minimal established web presence—and populate them with malicious, SEO-optimized content.

Hijacking Copilot Responses and User Trust

When users query Copilot about these niche topics, the RAG pipeline retrieves the attacker's malicious content, leading the AI assistant to deliver fraudulent instructions, hallucinated advice, or weaponized command-line snippets.

Defending AI Retrieval Pipelines

Securing AI assistants requires search result source reputation scoring, domain verification, and strict contextual guardrails on retrieved RAG sources.

talks.title: Reversing Approaches to Extract Embedded Scripts in macOS Malware
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle presents specialized reverse engineering techniques and tooling to automatically extract obfuscated AppleScript and shell payloads from macOS malware.
talks.summary:
Script-Based Malware in the macOS Threat Landscape

macOS malware authors increasingly utilize compiled AppleScript, JXA (JavaScript for Automation), and nested shell scripts to evade static antivirus signatures and execute living-off-the-land attacks.

Deconstructing Compiled AppleScript Binaries

Patrick Wardle analyzes the proprietary binary formats of compiled AppleScript (OSAX and .scpt components), explaining how malware authors obfuscate script bytecode and control-flow graphs.

Automating Dynamic and Static Script Extraction

Using custom reverse engineering tools and runtime hooking, analysts can intercept Apple Event dispatch routines, decompile bytecode, and recover original human-readable scripts in seconds.

Enhancing macOS Threat Triage

Automating script payload extraction significantly accelerates malware analysis workflows and enables defenders to generate rapid detection signatures for emerging macOS threats.

talks.title: Preventing One of The Largest Supply Chain Attacks in History
talks.teaser: Provides an in-depth breakdown of discovering and neutralizing the historic XZ Utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094) before stable Linux distribution deployment.
talks.summary:
The XZ Utils Supply-Chain Backdoor (CVE-2024-3094)

The XZ Utils compromise represents one of the most sophisticated multi-year open-source supply chain attacks in history, embedding a covert backdoor into upstream liblzma compression code.

Deconstructing the Multi-Stage Injection Mechanism

Maksim Shudrak provides a detailed technical breakdown of how the backdoor was concealed across obfuscated test files, injected during M4 build script execution, and hooked into OpenSSH authentication routines via IFUNC symbols.

Discovery, Reverse Engineering, and Neutralization

The talk chronicles the serendipitous discovery of anomalous CPU latency, rapid collaborative reverse engineering across the security community, and swift upstream neutralization before public releases reached stable Linux distributions.

Transforming Open-Source Supply Chain Security

Preventing future open-source supply chain compromises requires automated build artifact verification, reproducible builds, maintainer transparency, and enhanced funding for critical open-source infrastructure.

talks.teaser: Reveals an architectural vulnerability in cloud-managed enterprise VPNs that allowed unauthenticated administrative takeover and network pivoting across corporate tenants.
talks.summary:

Enterprises increasingly deploy cloud-managed VPN solutions to facilitate secure remote access for distributed workforces, relying on centralized SaaS dashboards for user provisioning and device policy enforcement.

Discovering Centralized Authentication Bypasses

David Cash and Rich Warren identify a critical architectural flaw in the cloud management control plane, where flawed SAML/OAuth session validation allowed unauthenticated attackers to elevate privileges to global tenant administrators.

National Tenant Compromise and Internal Network Pivoting

Hardening Cloud-Managed Network Infrastructure

Securing cloud VPN infrastructure requires enforcing strict tenant data isolation, conducting continuous cryptographic token validation, and mandating multi-party authorization for administrative configuration changes.

talks.title: Orion: Fuzzing Workflow Automation
talks.teaser: Introduces Orion, an automated fuzzing orchestration platform that streamlines harness generation, corpus management, and crash deduplication at enterprise scale.
talks.summary:
Scaling Modern Fuzzing Operations

Fuzzing is one of the most effective methods for discovering memory corruption and logic vulnerabilities in complex software. However, managing fuzzing campaigns at enterprise scale involves significant manual overhead.

Orion: Automated Fuzzing Orchestration

Max Bazalii and Marius Fleischer present Orion, an automated fuzzing management platform that automates harness synthesis, target instrumentations, seed corpus minimization, and dynamic scaling across cloud compute clusters.

Intelligent Crash Triage and Deduplication

Orion incorporates automated sanitizers, root-cause classification engines, and GDB/LLDB integration to triage crashing test cases and eliminate duplicate crash reports in real time.

Democratizing Automated Software Auditing

Deploying Orion empowers security teams and open-source developers to continuously audit software projects and remediate memory safety flaws before production release.

talks.title: Bypassing Intent Destination Checks, LaunchAnyWhere Privilege Escalation
talks.teaser: Demonstrates novel Intent redirection and LaunchAnyWhere privilege escalation techniques in modern Android platform frameworks.
talks.summary:
Android Inter-Process Communication and Intents

Android applications and system services rely on Intents to pass data and invoke activities across application boundaries, governed by strict component permission checks.

Bypassing Intent Destination Checks

Qidan He reveals novel parser discrepancies and state inconsistencies in modern Android OS frameworks that allow unprivileged third-party apps to bypass destination validation on PendingIntents.

Executing LaunchAnyWhere Privilege Escalation

Exploiting these Intent redirection flaws enables attackers to launch arbitrary unexported system activities, execute privileged background operations, and achieve full device compromise.

Remediation in Android Platform Frameworks

Securing Android IPC requires operating system updates enforcing explicit Intent matching and strict component permission boundaries.

talks.title: Ask EFF
talks.teaser: Electronic Frontier Foundation attorneys, technologists, and activists answer community questions on digital rights, surveillance law, privacy legislation, and AI policy.
talks.summary:
The Electronic Frontier Foundation and Digital Rights

The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) works to defend civil liberties, online privacy, free expression, and innovation in the digital world through legal advocacy, technological research, and grassroots activism.

Legal Trends in Surveillance and Encryption

EFF panelists break down current battles surrounding government mass surveillance, international encryption backdoors, biometric tracking regulations, and consumer data privacy laws.

Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Accountability

The panel addresses emerging legal challenges in artificial intelligence, copyright disputes over model training datasets, and automated algorithmic discrimination.

Community Q&A on Tech Policy

Panelists engage with the DEF CON community, answering questions on researcher legal protections (CFAA / DMCA Section 1201), right-to-repair initiatives, and digital defense strategies for activists.

talks.title: No VPN Needed? Cryptographic Attacks Against the OPC UA Protocol
talks.teaser: Discloses severe cryptographic implementation flaws in the OPC UA industrial communication standard, allowing adversaries to bypass encryption and spoof OT commands.
talks.summary:
The OPC UA Protocol in Industrial Automation

Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) is the dominant communication standard connecting industrial controllers, SCADA systems, and enterprise cloud applications, often marketed as secure enough to run without VPN isolation.

Auditing OPC UA Cryptographic Implementations

Tom Tervoort conducts an in-depth security analysis of OPC UA reference stacks, uncovering critical vulnerabilities in cryptographic handshake negotiation, digital certificate validation, and symmetric encryption padding.

Bypassing Message Authentication and Command Injection

Exploiting padding oracle flaws and key renegotiation weaknesses allows a network attacker to decrypt industrial control traffic, forge sensor telemetry, and inject unauthorized control commands into critical OT networks.

Hardening Industrial OPC UA Networks

Remediating OPC UA vulnerabilities requires vendor stack updates, enforcing strict certificate revocation checking, and maintaining network segmentation rather than relying solely on application-layer encryption.

talks.title: Killing Killnet
talks.teaser: Alex Holden shares exclusive intelligence on infiltrating, tracking, and disrupting the pro-Russian hacktivist syndicate Killnet.
talks.summary:
Investigating Pro-Russian Threat Actors

Alex Holden details extensive operational intelligence gathering targeting Killnet, a notorious pro-Russian hacktivist syndicate responsible for high-profile distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) campaigns across critical infrastructure worldwide.

Infiltration and Technical Attribution

Holden describes the technical methodologies used to identify Killnet operators, map their infrastructure networks, intercept internal communications, and uncover connections to state-aligned entities.

Disruption and Strategic Impact

The presentation reveals coordinated actions that successfully neutralized command channels, defanged tooling, and dismantled the group's reputation and threat capabilities.

talks.title: Reclaim Tech: A Community Movement
talks.teaser: Janet Vertesi and Andy Hull outline organizing strategies for technologists seeking ethical autonomy, digital rights, and collective community action.
talks.summary:
Building Grassroots Power in Technology

Janet Vertesi and Andy Hull examine the growing movement among engineers, researchers, and technologists to demand ethical accountability and exert collective leverage over surveillance and defense technologies.

Labor and Digital Activism Frameworks

The speakers provide case studies of workplace advocacy, whistleblowing protections, and community solidarity actions that have successfully steered tech projects toward the public interest.

Sustaining Community Momentum

The talk offers concrete toolkits for community building, coalition defense, and maintaining ethical integrity while working inside modern tech organizations.

talks.title: RATs & Socks: Abusing Google Services
talks.teaser: Valerio Alessandroni demonstrates how remote access trojans abuse trusted Google Cloud services and APIs for stealthy C2 communication and proxy tunneling.
talks.summary:
Weaponizing Legitimate Cloud Infrastructure

Valerio Alessandroni explores how adversaries increasingly rely on legitimate, trusted cloud platforms to bypass perimeter network defenses, egress filtering, and domain reputation checks.

Abusing Google Services for C2 and SOCKS Proxies

The presentation walks through the mechanics of converting Google Apps Script, Google Drive, and cloud endpoints into resilient command-and-control channels and dynamic SOCKS5 proxies.

Detection and Cloud Defense Countermeasures

Alessandroni provides defensive strategies, behavioral detection rules, and telemetry analysis techniques to spot anomalous cloud API interactions inside enterprise networks.

talks.title: Planting C4: Cross-Compatible External C2 for Your Implants
talks.teaser: Scott Taylor introduces C4, an open-source framework decoupling payload implants from command-and-control protocols using versatile external connectors.
talks.summary:
Architectural Bottlenecks in Modern C2 Frameworks

Scott Taylor analyzes the limitations of traditional red team implants that tightly couple execution logic to specific transport protocols, making evasion adaptation difficult during active operations.

Introducing the C4 Modular Connector Architecture

The talk introduces C4, an extensible open-source framework that separates implant execution from transport layers, enabling live protocol swapping across arbitrary channels (DNS, WebSockets, cloud storage, or social media).

Practical Demonstrations and Operator Integration

Taylor demonstrates deploying cross-platform implants with custom connectors and provides guidance on integrating C4 with existing offensive toolsets and testing defensive resilience.

talks.title: Loading Models, Launching Shells: Abusing AI File Formats for Code Execution
talks.teaser: C Parzian analyzes weaponized machine learning file formats, demonstrating arbitrary code execution vectors in widely deployed AI frameworks.
talks.summary:
The Blind Trust in AI Model Weights

C Parzian investigates the rampant assumption of trust when data scientists and developers download pretrained neural network model weights from open-source repositories and public hubs.

Dissecting Dangerous Model Formats

The presentation uncovers unsafe deserialization vulnerabilities, embedded script execution, and parser flaws across popular serialization formats including Pickle, PyTorch checkpoints, and custom tensor structures.

Exploitation Scenarios and Defensive Hardening

Parzian demonstrates realistic supply chain attack chains executing arbitrary shells upon model load and presents best practices for safe loading using formats like SafeTensors and isolated sandboxing.

talks.title: Off-Grid Datarunning in Oppressive Regimes: Sneakernet and PirateBox
talks.teaser: Robert Menes explores resilient off-grid communication technologies, physical sneakernets, and local PirateBox nodes operating under heavy censorship.
talks.summary:
Information Resistance in Disconnected Environments

Robert Menes analyzes operational tactics used by activists, journalists, and citizens in regions experiencing internet blackouts, nationwide firewalls, and aggressive telecommunications surveillance.

Modern Sneakernets and Hardware Dropboxes

The presentation explores deploying air-gapped PirateBox systems, portable wireless dead drops, and sneakernet workflows using encrypted removable media to share news and software safely.

Operational Security and Physical Concealment

Menes shares practical operational security protocols for courier transport, device sanitization, and tamper-resistant storage to minimize risk under hostile physical scrutiny.

talks.title: Quiet Confidence: An Introvert's Journey to Technical Public Speaking
talks.teaser: Emma Fang shares actionable frameworks and personal strategies for introverted engineers to overcome public speaking anxiety and share technical research.
talks.summary:
Bridging Deep Technical Research and Public Presentations

Emma Fang addresses the common dilemma faced by introverted cybersecurity researchers whose valuable technical work remains unshared due to public speaking apprehension and impostor syndrome.

Cognitive and Practical Presentation Strategies

The talk outlines practical rehearsal methods, slide structuring techniques, and energy management strategies specifically designed for naturally quiet or introverted individuals.

Empowering Inclusive Community Voices

Fang encourages technical conferences and mentorship groups to build more supportive speaking environments that welcome diverse communication styles.

talks.title: 40 Years of Phrack: Hacking, Zines & Digital Dissent
talks.teaser: Editors and contributors celebrate four decades of Phrack magazine, reviewing foundational exploit techniques, hacker journalism, and counterculture history.
talks.summary:
Four Decades of Foundational Hacker Publishing

Staff editors and prominent contributors celebrate the 40th anniversary of Phrack, the underground electronic magazine that shaped modern computer security, reverse engineering, and exploit development.

From Phreaking to Modern Memory Corruption

The panel reflects on seminal articles that defined entire eras of cybersecurity, from early phreaking and stack smashing (Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit) to cutting-edge hypervisor and kernel exploitation.

Preserving Hacker Ethos and Independent Research

The discussion explores how Phrack has maintained editorial independence, high technical standards, and an irreverent hacker spirit across shifting generations of technology and commercialization.
